nodes.name: Intel Loihi 1
nodes.summary: First-generation Intel neuromorphic research chip (14 nm, 128 cores, up to 131,072 neurons); native CUBA-LIF neuron with hard reset-to-zero, requiring a two-compartment trick for reset-by-subtraction. Superseded by Loihi 2 and now accessible only through the discontinued NxSDK/NxTF software path.

attributes.time_model: Fixed-size, globally synchronized discrete timesteps via asynchronous barrier-message handshakes across the NoC; wall-clock duration per timestep varies with spike traffic, not fixed.
attributes.neuron_models: Two-stage cascaded discrete-time CUBA-LIF (current-based leaky integrate-and-fire).
attributes.reset_semantics: Native hard reset-to-zero only. Reset-by-subtraction achieved only via a two-compartment workaround (NxTF compiler), doubling neuron/compartment cost.
attributes.payload: Binary spike by default; optional graded (multi-bit) payload existed in the 32-bit message format but was not the idiomatic mode.
attributes.weight_precision: 1-9 bits, signed, mixable within a neuron's fan-out.
attributes.on_chip_learning: Programmable microcode learning engine per core: pairwise STDP, triplet STDP, reward-modulated synaptic tagging.
attributes.operator_coverage: NxTF compiler supports input, flatten, average, concat, dense, pool, conv layer types with CUBA-LIF compartment parameters; up to 9-bit weight precision.
attributes.toolchain: NxSDK / NxTF (Keras-derived compiler), discontinued; Intel redirects INRC members to Lava since 2022.
attributes.availability: Not commercially available; INRC membership required (research/evaluation only), cloud access via Neuromorphic Research Cloud.
attributes.price: Not sold; access only via INRC membership.

nodes.name: Intel Loihi 2
nodes.summary: Second-generation Intel neuromorphic chip (Intel 4 process, up to 1M neurons/chip) with a fully microcode-programmable neuron engine and native graded (up to 32-bit signed payload) spikes, enabling sigma-delta and Resonate-and-Fire neurons beyond CUBA-LIF. Its software stack (Lava/Lava-DL/NetX) was archived by Intel around 2026-05-13 with no announced successor.

attributes.time_model: Same barrier-synchronized global algorithmic timestep model as Loihi 1; supports pipelined (throughput-optimized) and fall-through (latency-optimized) execution modes.
attributes.neuron_models: Fully microcode-programmable: CUBA-LIF, Resonate-and-Fire, Izhikevich, sigma-delta, Hopf resonators.
attributes.reset_semantics: Native reset is hard-to-zero (v reset to 0 on spike) per the reference LIF equations; reset-by-subtraction is not documented as a first-class microcode primitive, and no equivalent of the Loihi-1 two-compartment soft-reset workaround was found documented for Loihi 2/Lava.
attributes.payload: Graded spikes with up to 32-bit signed integer architectural payload field (individual projects typically configure down to 8, 16, or 24 bits).
attributes.weight_precision: 8-bit synaptic weights by default (extendable to 8n-bit via chained synapses); other projects report 8-bit with 4 fractional bits.
attributes.state_precision: Variable, 0-4096 bytes/neuron depending on neuron model (vs. fixed 24 bytes on Loihi 1); Compartment state registers report up to 64-bit capacity composed of 8/16/24-bit sub-fields.
attributes.on_chip_learning: Three-factor (neuromodulated) learning via arbitrary microcode-computed modulatory terms; demonstrated in Lava simulation (R-STDP) with on-chip execution stated as forthcoming, not confirmed on physical silicon in the sources reviewed.
attributes.operator_coverage: Lava-DL NetX HDF5 schema: input, flatten, average, concat, dense, pool, conv, default neuron CUBA-LIF; also demonstrated Resonate-and-Fire, sigma-delta, aLIF via custom microcode process models.
attributes.toolchain: Lava / Lava-DL (SLAYER 2.0, Bootstrap, NetX) - archived by Intel as of 2026-05-13; successor SDK unannounced.
attributes.availability: Not commercially available for the general public; obtainable only via INRC membership (Oheo Gulch single-chip and Kapoho Point 8-chip boards); commercial/government orgs can purchase an on-site Kapoho Point system.
attributes.price: Not publicly listed; gated behind INRC membership and Intel evaluation.

nodes.name: SpiNNaker 1
nodes.summary: Manycore ARM968-based digital neuromorphic manycore system (18 cores/chip, GALS architecture, up to ~1.04M cores at full 10-cabinet scale) that simulates arbitrary software-defined neuron models at a default 1 ms real-time timestep, communicating via best-effort (drop-possible) AER packets over a custom asynchronous router fabric.

attributes.time_model: Discrete timer-interrupt timestep, default 1 ms (biologically real-time convention, not a hardware floor); sub-millisecond timesteps possible at proportional real-time-factor cost.
attributes.neuron_models: Fully software-defined via C code (sPyNNaker neural_modelling library): current/conductance-based LIF, Izhikevich, plus plugin models.
attributes.reset_semantics: Not hard-wired; achievable as either hard or soft reset via a user-definable neuron_model_has_spiked() callback, but not a sPyNNaker built-in default (built-in cell types like IF_curr_exp use PyNN-conventional hard-reset LIF/IF).
attributes.payload: Binary AER spike packets (40- or 72-bit) carrying source-neuron ID; no guaranteed delivery (packets can be re-routed late or dropped under congestion).
attributes.weight_precision: Fixed-point only (no FPU on ARM968); Q-format fixed point commonly used (e.g., Q6.16 in one deep-belief-network implementation).
attributes.on_chip_learning: STDP and structural plasticity supported in sPyNNaker's neuron/synapse model library.
attributes.operator_coverage: General-purpose PyNN neuron/synapse simulator, not a native CNN-layer framework; convolutional structure must be expressed as ordinary projections (e.g., via SNN Toolbox's build_convolution).
attributes.toolchain: sPyNNaker (PyNN backend) + SpiNNTools (partition/place/route/load/execute/extract pipeline).
attributes.availability: Hosted at University of Manchester (up to ~1.04M-core machine) plus standalone 4-/48-chip boards; free EBRAINS-account access for evaluation/basic research.
attributes.price: Not sold as a product; free access via EBRAINS Collaboratory account for research.

nodes.name: SpiNNaker 2
nodes.summary: Successor chip (22 nm FDSOI, ARM Cortex-M4F cores with FPU, 144 PEs/chip) adding a 16x4 INT8 MAC accelerator per processing element for hybrid dense-ANN/spiking execution; commercialized by SpiNNcloud Systems and deployed at multi-billion-neuron scale (Dresden, Sandia, Leipzig).

attributes.time_model: Same SpiNNaker-style discrete-timestep, software-programmable model as SpiNNaker 1, extended with fine-grained per-PE DVFS/adaptive body biasing.
attributes.neuron_models: Software-defined on Cortex-M4F cores (LIF/CuBa-LIF standard); py-spinnaker2's NIR importer supports Conv1d, Conv2d, Flatten, Affine, Linear, CuBaLIF, IF, LIF, SumPool2d.
attributes.reset_semantics: py-spinnaker2 backend supports BOTH reset-by-subtraction and reset-to-zero for IF/LIF/CuBa-LIF -- a hardware/software capability broader than what the formal NIR primitive spec itself exposes.
attributes.payload: Supports large (128-bit) packet payloads; EventProp backward-pass demo transmits signed floating-point error-gradient values as packet payloads, distinct from ordinary binary forward spikes.
attributes.weight_precision: 8-bit signed synapse weights (py-spinnaker2 deployed configuration); MAC accelerator supports 8/16-bit MAC with 8/16/32-bit output.
attributes.state_precision: 32-bit floating-point neuron state/parameters (mixed precision: quantized weights, float32 dynamics).
attributes.operator_coverage: Hybrid SNN/DNN execution: same PE runs event-driven spiking code and, via the MAC array, dense 8/16-bit convolution/matmul for conventional DNN layers.
attributes.toolchain: py-spinnaker2 (PyNN-inspired API), NIR importer, Brian2-based software-emulation fallback.
attributes.availability: Commercially deployed via SpiNNcloud Systems (Dresden half-scale system, Sandia National Labs, University of Leipzig); largest system stood up ~30,000 chips as of mid-2025 (vendor statement).
attributes.price: Sold as commercial supercomputing systems/racks; per-chip/per-board pricing not published.

nodes.name: SynSense Speck
nodes.summary: Fully asynchronous, clockless SoC integrating a 128x128 on-chip Dynamic Vision Sensor with the DYNAP-CNN convolutional neuromorphic processor (9 fixed conv->IF->pool cores, up to ~328K neurons). Measured sub-4-microsecond end-to-end 9-layer propagation latency, with reset-by-subtraction as the documented hardware default.

attributes.time_model: Fully asynchronous, no global or local clock for the compute pipeline; computation triggered directly by event arrival (request/acknowledge circuit blocks). Speck2e+ has an optional slow clock for leak/DVS-filter/readout-averaging only, not the conv/IF compute path.
attributes.neuron_models: Nonleaky Integrate-and-Fire (IAFSqueeze) by default; optional leak requires a bias term plus slow-clock configuration.
attributes.reset_semantics: Native, hardware-configurable reset-by-subtraction is the documented default (return_to_zero=False); hard reset available via return_to_zero=True.
attributes.payload: Binary AER spike events with layer/x/y/feature/timestamp fields (microsecond resolution).
attributes.weight_precision: 8-bit fixed point.
attributes.on_chip_learning: unknown (Speck line has no documented on-chip learning path; contrast SynSense's earlier DYNAP-SE analog line)
attributes.operator_coverage: 9 configurable cores, each conv(kernel up to 16x16, stride {1,2,4,8}, padding 0-7)->IF->optional sum-pooling only (AvgPool2d auto-rewritten to SumPool2d); Linear auto-converted to 1x1 Conv2d; no native BatchNorm; uniform per-layer threshold only (no per-neuron thresholds); fan-out of 2 destination cores per core.
attributes.host_interface: SPI/serial I/O, interrupt pins for up to 15+1 classes; USB 3.1 host connection for the Dev Kit.
attributes.toolchain: Sinabs (from_model/DynapcnnNetwork) -> samna runtime.
attributes.availability: Speck Dev Kit and Demo Kit are purchasable/orderable hardware products, no research-membership gate (unlike Loihi/INRC).
attributes.price: List pricing not publicly posted ("available only on application"); Speck Demo Kit early-bird batch reported around $199 (trade press).

nodes.name: SynSense DYNAP-CNN
nodes.summary: Standalone predecessor processor core to Speck (12 mm^2, 22 nm, over 1M Integrate-and-Fire neurons, 4M programmable parameters), scalable via daisy-chained devices; the same asynchronous, clockless, sub-5 ms latency architecture minus the integrated DVS sensor.

attributes.time_model: Fully asynchronous, no high-speed clock; computation triggered directly by AER event arrival, sub-5 ms latency.
attributes.neuron_models: Nonleaky Integrate-and-Fire, same conv->IF->pool per-core template as Speck.
attributes.reset_semantics: Reset-by-subtraction is Sinabs's documented default (MembraneSubtract()); matches Speck's hardware behavior.
attributes.payload: Binary AER spike events.
attributes.weight_precision: 8-bit fixed point (consistent with the Speck/DYNAP-CNN family).
attributes.operator_coverage: Same conv->IF->pool per-core template as Speck; no native BatchNorm; AvgPool2d not natively supported.
attributes.toolchain: Sinabs -> samna.
attributes.availability: Devkit historically available (2019 announcement); largely superseded by Speck in current SynSense product listings.

nodes.name: SynSense Xylo
nodes.summary: Separate SynSense digital SNN inference ASIC family for audio/IMU/low-dimensional sensory signals (XyloAudio 2/3, XyloIMU), genuinely clocked and synchronous (up to 50-100 MHz internal clock, global timestep dt), with native subtractive reset and up to 31 output spikes per neuron per timestep.

attributes.time_model: Synchronous, time-stepped architecture with a global hardware clock/timestep dt (up to 50-100 MHz internal); genuinely one hardware update per dt, unlike the asynchronous Speck/DYNAP-CNN line.
attributes.neuron_models: Current-based LIF (CUBA-LIF) with per-neuron/per-synapse configurable time constants, up to two synaptic states per hidden neuron.
attributes.reset_semantics: Subtractive reset is a fixed hardware property ("Reset during event generation is performed by subtraction"), not a software-switchable option.
attributes.payload: Up to 31 spikes/timestep for hidden neurons, 1 for output neurons -- deviates from the single-spike-per-step assumption of most conversion theory.
attributes.weight_precision: 8-bit weights.
attributes.operator_coverage: Up to ~1000 hidden neurons (XyloAudio 2) / 992 (XyloAudio 3) / 496 (XyloIMU); 8-32 output channels; 16 input event channels; ~124-150 KB on-chip memory.
attributes.toolchain: Rockpool (mapper() -> quantize_methods -> config_from_specification()) -> XyloSamna/XyloMonitor.
attributes.availability: Commercially orderable Dev Kits (pricing on application); no research-membership gate.

nodes.name: BrainScaleS-1
nodes.summary: Heidelberg wafer-scale analog neuromorphic system (HICANN ASICs, 512 neurons/chip, ~10,000x accelerated analog time constants) that physically emulates AdEx/LIF neuron circuits rather than numerically simulating them; requires per-neuron calibration for manufacturing mismatch and hardware-in-the-loop training to reach usable accuracy for converted networks.

attributes.time_model: Physical analog circuit time, running ~10,000x faster than biological real time (component values, not digital clock cycles, set the acceleration factor).
attributes.neuron_models: Analog AdEx/LIF emulated in HICANN circuits.
attributes.reset_semantics: Not confirmed as reset-by-subtraction in sources reviewed; analog reset behavior calibrated per neuron.
attributes.payload: unknown
attributes.weight_precision: 4-bit hardware weights used in the documented rate-coded conversion experiment (coarser than BrainScaleS-2's 6-bit).
attributes.operator_coverage: unknown
attributes.toolchain: PyNN (pynn.brainscales / neuromorphic hardware backend) via EBRAINS platform.
attributes.availability: Free remote access via EBRAINS (evaluation/basic research); not commercially purchasable.
attributes.price: Not sold; free EBRAINS remote access.

nodes.name: BrainScaleS-2
nodes.summary: Heidelberg single-chip analog neuromorphic ASIC (65 nm, 512 neurons x 512 synapses, two embedded digital plasticity processors) running ~1000x accelerated analog dynamics, with a non-spiking "hagen" MAC mode and a spiking LIF/AdEx mode; both require calibration plus hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) training because fixed-pattern mismatch and trial-to-trial analog noise prevent exact correspondence to a software IF/LIF model.

attributes.time_model: Physical analog circuit time at ~1000x biological acceleration; experiments scheduled into fixed wall-clock frames by an on-chip digital plasticity processor (PPU), with an explicit ~100-500 ns input interval in the non-spiking ("hagen") mode.
attributes.neuron_models: Full AdEx (adaptive exponential integrate-and-fire), reduces to LIF with adaptation disabled; native, extensively documented multi-compartment support for genuine dendritic computation.
attributes.reset_semantics: Native AdEx circuit performs hard reset (clamped to reset potential Vr for a refractory period on spike). No source describes a native or multi-compartment-workaround reset-by-subtraction mode.
attributes.payload: unknown
attributes.weight_precision: 6-bit signed synaptic weight ([-63,63]); 5-bit unsigned input resolution and 8-bit output (ADC) resolution in non-spiking "hagen" mode.
attributes.state_precision: Calibration equalizes synaptic strength to ~7% precision across 512 neurons; pre-calibration mismatch can reduce effective weight resolution from 6-bit to ~4-bit.
attributes.on_chip_learning: Hybrid plasticity: analog correlation measurement (CADC) plus digital plasticity-rule computation on the PPU; demonstrated reward-modulated STDP, homeostatic plasticity, structural plasticity.
attributes.operator_coverage: Automatic partitioning of networks exceeding a single chip's 256x512 synapse array onto multiple chips (hxtorch).
attributes.toolchain: hxtorch (perceptron/MAC mode and hxtorch.snn spiking mode), PyNN (pynn_brainscales.brainscales2), calix calibration library.
attributes.availability: Free remote access via EBRAINS (evaluation/basic research, queued jobs, SLURM-based scheduling); not commercially purchasable.
attributes.price: Not sold; free EBRAINS remote access.

nodes.name: IBM TrueNorth
nodes.summary: Fully digital, event-driven neurosynaptic chip (28 nm, 4096 cores, 1M neurons, 256M synapses, ~65-70 mW) evaluated once per 1 kHz global "tick"; its Eedn training/deployment methodology encodes activation magnitude spatially across redundant trinary-weighted neuron copies within a single tick, not via multi-timestep temporal rate accumulation. Discontinued; superseded conceptually by the non-spiking NorthPole NPU.

attributes.time_model: Global 1 kHz synchronization signal ("tick"); all neurons evaluated once per tick; whole-network evaluation completes within one tick for the Eedn deployment methodology ("one classification per hardware tick").
attributes.neuron_models: Configurable augmented IF model (23 parameters), deterministic/stochastic leak, positive and negative thresholds, reproduces all 20 Izhikevich behavior classes via 1-3 simple neuron instances.
attributes.reset_semantics: Natively configurable: "normal mode" (hard reset to Rj), "linear mode" (reset-by-subtraction, residual potential above threshold retained), and a stochastic non-reset mode -- reset-by-subtraction is first-class hardware-native.
attributes.payload: 1-bit binary spikes only; no native multi-bit/graded payload.
attributes.weight_precision: No native multi-bit weight; trinary weights ({-1,0,+1}) constructed via a pair of neuron copies over a 4-entry axon-type lookup table mapping to signed integers in [-255,255].
attributes.on_chip_learning: None; inference-only, all training (Eedn) happens off-chip.
attributes.operator_coverage: 256 input axons x 256x256 binary synaptic crossbar x 256 neurons per core, time-multiplexed; whole-network mapped across up to 4096 cores/chip.
attributes.toolchain: Eedn (backprop training with trinary weights + triangle-function surrogate) -> Corelet compiler -> NS1e/NS16e boards.
attributes.availability: Not commercially available; discontinued since mid-2010s DARPA SyNAPSE era, distributed only to a limited research ecosystem (30+ institutions).

nodes.name: IBM NorthPole
nodes.summary: IBM's 2023 successor architecture (12 nm, 22B transistors, 256 cores, 192 MB distributed SRAM) explicitly described by IBM as an extension of TrueNorth, but purely digital, low-precision (8/4/2-bit) MAC-based inference NPU with no spiking/event-driven neuron model or membrane potential dynamics -- efficiency gains derive from memory-locality and low-bit MAC execution, not event-driven temporal sparsity.

attributes.time_model: Not applicable; conventional synchronous digital dataflow, not an event/spike time model.
attributes.neuron_models: None; not a spiking architecture -- standard 8/4/2-bit MAC operations.
attributes.reset_semantics: Not applicable.
attributes.payload: Not applicable (no spike events).
attributes.operator_coverage: 16x16 array of cores linked by two on-chip networks; up to 2048/4096/8192 int8/int4/int2 ops per core per cycle at ~400 MHz nominal.
attributes.toolchain: Conventional DNN inference toolchain, not a spiking-network toolchain.
attributes.availability: Deployed as a PCIe accelerator card, benchmarked against GPU/CPU on ResNet-50/YOLOv4.

nodes.name: Tsinghua Tianjic
nodes.summary: Many-core, reconfigurable hybrid chip explicitly designed to run both ANNs and SNNs on the same silicon using a shared axon/synapse/dendrite/soma/router abstraction; demonstrated driving an unmanned bicycle performing simultaneous real-time perception and control tasks. Commercial lineage continues via Lynxi's KA200/HP300 products.

attributes.time_model: SNN-mode FCores use spike-event/temporal dynamics with membrane integration, threshold crossing, and reset; ANN-mode FCores instead refresh weighted activations every cycle with no persistent temporal state -- both coexist per-core.
attributes.neuron_models: SNN-mode FCores support spiking neuron dynamics; some FCores can relay full-precision non-spiking membrane potentials between dendritic compartments in "ANN mode", improving large-scale-SNN accuracy by 11.5 percentage points over an SNN-only configuration.
attributes.reset_semantics: unknown
attributes.payload: unknown
attributes.weight_precision: unknown
attributes.operator_coverage: Reconfigurable axon/synapse/dendrite/soma/router building blocks shared between ANN and SNN modes.
attributes.toolchain: First-generation automatic model-mapping/compiling toolchain (Tsinghua); commercial descendant is Lynxi's BIDL/Lyngor/LynSDK stack.
attributes.availability: Research chip (2019 Nature paper); commercial lineage continues through Lynxi Technologies spinout products.

nodes.name: Lynxi KA200
nodes.summary: Commercial compute-in-memory, many-core heterogeneous-fusion chip from Lynxi (spinout building on the Tianjic lineage), natively supporting both deep-learning ANNs and brain-inspired SNNs with mixed-precision compute; deployment path (BIDL/Lyngor/LynSDK) is effectively unavailable outside mainland China per sources reviewed.

attributes.time_model: Timestep-driven: BIDL documentation states "a timestep iteration is located outside the neural network," i.e. the device computes all layers for one timestep then advances (contrast with SpikingJelly-style layer-internal timestep loops).
attributes.neuron_models: LIF and "LIF+" (spike-firing and analog-value-firing variants) by default in BIDL; supports custom user-defined neuron classes.
attributes.reset_semantics: unknown -- not documented explicitly in sources reviewed
attributes.payload: unknown
attributes.weight_precision: unknown
attributes.operator_coverage: 250,000 neurons/25,000,000 synapses per chip in dense mode, up to 2,000,000 neurons/2,000,000,000 synapses in sparse mode; 48 TOPS@INT8 / 24 TFLOPS@FP16 per chip.
attributes.toolchain: BIDL (PyTorch-based training/deployment framework) -> Lyngor compiler -> LynSDK runtime; batch size 1 only on-chip; training requires GPU, only inference targets the chip.
attributes.availability: Commercially available in China (HP300/KA200/edge boxes); NOT FOUND evidence of availability, distribution, or benchmarking outside mainland China.

nodes.name: BrainChip Akida
nodes.summary: Commercial neuromorphic NSoC family (AKD1000/AKD1500/Akida 2.0 IP/Akida Pico) whose converted-CNN deployment path (CNN2SNN/QuantizeML) collapses to a single feedforward pass over quantized, integer-only activations with a static per-neuron threshold that has absorbed folded BatchNorm scale/shift -- not a multi-timestep rate-coded IF/LIF accumulation. Lineage traces genuinely to Thorpe's rank-order-coding research (Spikenet Technology acquisition, 2016), but the order-sensitive shunting-inhibition mechanism has not been shown to operate inside converted-CNN hidden layers.

attributes.time_model: No user-exposed multi-timestep simulation horizon T for the standard converted-CNN path; execution is a single feedforward pass. Some layer types (BufferTempConv, TENN blocks) carry an internal temporal buffer for genuinely sequential data, a different notion of time.
attributes.neuron_models: Integrate-and-(single-)fire, no leak, no exposed decay constant on the standard path; circuit-level description matches classical IF design, but the multi-step "repeat" is absent in the converted-CNN deployment.
attributes.reset_semantics: Not reset-by-subtraction in the classical sense: threshold is a static comparator with the quantization rounding offset and folded BatchNorm scale/shift baked in once at conversion time, not an iterative subtract-and-carry loop across timesteps.
attributes.payload: Not necessarily binary -- BrainChip states events "can have a value that indicates neural behavior" -- except the mandatory 1-bit Edge-Learning FullyConnected layer.
attributes.weight_precision: 1/2/4/8-bit depending on layer type and Akida version (Akida 1.0: InputConv 8-bit weights, Conv/Dense 1/2/4-bit; Akida 2.0 IP: 8/4/1-bit; Edge-Learning layer: 1-bit mandatory).
attributes.on_chip_learning: "Akida Edge Learning": restricted to the last layer only, must be FullyConnected with 1-bit weights and 1-bit input; competitive/homeostatic Hebbian-style AkidaUnsupervised optimizer; only supported on Akida 1.0 as of current MetaTF docs.
attributes.operator_coverage: Akida 1.0: InputConvolutional, Convolutional, SeparableConvolutional, Dense (feed-forward only, strict ordering/padding/stride rules). Akida 2.0: adds Attention, VitEncoderBlock, BufferTempConv, MadNorm, Shiftmax, etc.
attributes.host_interface: AKD1000: PCIe 2.1 x2, USB 3.0, I3C/I2S/UART/JTAG. AKD1500: PCIe Gen2 + SPI. Akida Pico: SPI only, standalone (no host CPU required).
attributes.toolchain: MetaTF: QuantizeML (quantization-aware training/PTQ) -> CNN2SNN (convert() -> .fbz) -> Akida runtime (hardware or software simulator).
attributes.availability: Commercially purchasable: AKD1000 PCIe dev board $289, Raspberry Pi kits $995-$1,495; AKD1500 commercial shipments began June 2026 (~2,000 units shipped by Aug 2026, yield issues under investigation).
attributes.price: AKD1000 PCIe dev board $289; AKD1500 PCIe commercial-temp 5-pack $199.99 (~$40/chip).

nodes.name: MorphIC
nodes.summary: UCLouvain academic quad-core, binary-weight digital neuromorphic ASIC (65 nm, 738k synapses/mm^2, stochastic spike-driven online learning) that provides the clearest controlled, same-silicon comparison of rate coding versus rank-order coding energy cost on the identical MNIST task.

attributes.time_model: Fully event-driven digital design; max clock 55 MHz (0.8V) / 210 MHz (1.2V).
attributes.neuron_models: LIF, 2,048 neurons across 4 cores.
attributes.reset_semantics: unknown -- not explicitly restated as hard vs. subtractive in sources reviewed (SDSP-driven reset behavior, not the standard IF hard/subtractive framing)
attributes.payload: Binary spikes.
attributes.weight_precision: 1-bit (binary) synapses, >2M plastic synapses.
attributes.operator_coverage: unknown
attributes.toolchain: unknown
attributes.availability: Academic research chip (UCLouvain), not commercially sold.

nodes.name: DYNAP-SE2
nodes.summary: SynSense/INI Zurich mixed-signal analog neuromorphic ASIC (1024 analog AdExpIF neurons in 2x2 16x16-neuron cores, 4-bit configurable synaptic weight); its own companion simulator DynapSim explicitly does not numerically match the hardware, and no rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion pipeline for this chip was located in the sources reviewed.

attributes.time_model: Fully analog, asynchronous, subthreshold-operated circuits; no global clock.
attributes.neuron_models: 1024 analog AdExpIF (adaptive exponential integrate-and-fire) neurons, 4 dendritic branches, 64 synapses each.
attributes.reset_semantics: unknown
attributes.payload: Digital spike output only; membrane potential is not directly accessible ("there is no easy way to access thousands of analog values at the same time").
attributes.weight_precision: 4-bit configurable synaptic weight.
attributes.operator_coverage: unknown
attributes.toolchain: Rockpool DynapSim (approximate, explicitly non-hardware-exact simulator).
attributes.availability: Commercially available via SynSense.

nodes.name: Innatera Pulsar
nodes.summary: Commercial mixed-signal neuromorphic microcontroller (TSMC 28 nm, 2Q25 production) integrating both an analog SNN engine and a separate digital SNN engine alongside an INT8 CNN accelerator and a RISC-V core; marketed as ultra-low-power always-on edge sensing. All quantitative performance claims located in this research are vendor-sourced, with no independent third-party peer-reviewed benchmark found.

attributes.time_model: unknown
attributes.neuron_models: Analog SNN engine (capacitor-based neuron-state storage, 16K-parameter capacity) and digital SNN engine (49K-parameter capacity), same design principles implemented in each domain.
attributes.reset_semantics: unknown -- not documented in sources reviewed
attributes.payload: unknown
attributes.weight_precision: unknown
attributes.operator_coverage: Also includes a 32-MAC/cycle INT8 CNN accelerator and an FFT/IFFT accelerator alongside the two SNN engines.
attributes.toolchain: Talamo SDK (PyTorch extension: spike encoders/decoders, e.g. IFEncoder, MaxRateDecoder; pipe.to(innatera_soc) device deployment).
attributes.availability: Commercially available (production shipments 2Q25 per vendor).

nodes.name: Cerebron
nodes.summary: FPGA-based reconfigurable architecture (Xilinx XC7Z100, 200 MHz) explicitly built around the SNN Toolbox / Rueckauer-Diehl ANN-to-SNN conversion methodology, targeting spatiotemporal sparsity in standard, depthwise, and pointwise convolutions with an online channel-wise workload scheduler.

attributes.time_model: Clock-driven synchronous FPGA execution at 200 MHz.
attributes.neuron_models: Converted via SNN Toolbox methodology (implies IF, standard reset-by-subtraction per that toolbox's convention, but this is not independently restated in Cerebron's own text).
attributes.reset_semantics: Not explicitly restated in Cerebron's own text -- inherited from SNNtoolbox's convention.
attributes.payload: Binary spikes.
attributes.weight_precision: unknown
attributes.operator_coverage: Standard, depthwise, and pointwise convolution with reconfigurable inter/intra-compute-unit sparsity exploitation.
attributes.toolchain: SNN Toolbox (offline conversion) -> Cerebron RTL/bitstream.
attributes.availability: Academic FPGA implementation, not a commercial product.

nodes.name: APEX
nodes.summary: RTL/cycle-level-simulated accelerator (Synopsys Design Compiler, 40 nm, 400 MHz) that integrates the PASC-IF neuron from the PASCAL conversion algorithm into the LoAS accelerator framework as a fully combinational circuit, targeting mixed INT4/INT8 precision and dual (spike + weight) sparsity. Not fabricated silicon.

attributes.time_model: Fully-temporal-parallel dataflow (inherited from LoAS): resolves the entire post-synaptic input tensor across all T timesteps before invoking the neuron unit, removing the temporal loop-carried dependency of sequential PASC-IF execution.
attributes.neuron_models: PASC-IF (spike-accumulation, adaptive layerwise activation IF neuron), soft reset, explicit inhibitory (negative) spikes.
attributes.reset_semantics: Soft reset (not classical reset-by-subtraction), with inhibitory spikes as part of the mechanism.
attributes.payload: Signed (inhibitory) spikes supported, a departure from the binary-only convention of most FPGA accelerators surveyed.
attributes.weight_precision: Mixed INT4/INT8 via split processing-element array.
attributes.operator_coverage: 16 TPPEs (split INT4/INT8), 256 KB double-buffered global cache, 128 GB/s HBM off-chip model.
attributes.toolchain: PASCAL (algorithm) -> APEX (RTL synthesis/cycle simulation).
attributes.availability: Not fabricated; RTL synthesis and cycle-level simulation result only.

nodes.name: SyncNN
nodes.summary: FPGA-based (Xilinx ZCU102/ZCU104/ZED, physical boards) rate-encoding IF accelerator that mathematically proves a synchronous reformulation of standard multi-timestep asynchronous IF+reset-by-subtraction execution: only the Poisson input-encoding layer runs for the full T-step window, downstream layers compute the equivalent spike count in one shot via Vm/Vth division.

attributes.time_model: Synchronous, clock-driven FPGA execution; input-layer Poisson encoding still needs the full T-step window, downstream layers run once per inference.
attributes.neuron_models: Explicit IF model.
attributes.reset_semantics: Explicit, native reset-by-subtraction (Vm[o] -= Vth), proven mathematically equivalent to the standard iterative threshold-and-subtract execution.
attributes.payload: Binary spikes; Poisson-rate input encoding.
attributes.weight_precision: 16/8/4-bit configurable.
attributes.operator_coverage: LeNet, Network-in-Network, and VGG architectures evaluated (MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10).
attributes.toolchain: Vitis HLS/SDSoC hardware-mode build.
attributes.availability: Academic FPGA implementation (open-source), not a commercial product.

nodes.name: NeuroFlex
nodes.summary: RTL/cycle-level-simulated accelerator (Synopsys Design Compiler, 40 nm, 560 MHz) extending PASCAL's layer-level lossless ANN/SNN equivalence to column-level hybrid execution, where individual output columns within one layer independently run in ANN mode or PASC-IF SNN mode chosen by a profiling-driven scheduler. Not fabricated silicon.

attributes.time_model: Column-granularity hybrid ANN/SNN scheduling within a fully-temporal-parallel dataflow, inherited from the same family as APEX.
attributes.neuron_models: PASC-IF (spike-accumulation IF neuron), soft reset.
attributes.reset_semantics: Soft reset (not classical reset-by-subtraction), inherited from PASCAL's PASC-IF formulation.
attributes.payload: unknown
attributes.weight_precision: Unified INT8 format for all intermediate activations regardless of ANN/SNN execution mode per column.
attributes.operator_coverage: Evaluated on VGG-16, ResNet-34, GoogLeNet, and BERT.
attributes.toolchain: PASCAL (algorithm) -> NeuroFlex (RTL synthesis/cycle simulation, CACTI 7.0 memory modeling).
attributes.availability: Not fabricated; RTL synthesis and cycle-level simulation result only.

nodes.name: FPGA SNN accelerators (general)
nodes.summary: General-purpose FPGA family used across the survey for custom SNN accelerator implementations (SyncNN, Spiker/Spiker+, FireFly/v2, Cerebron, and others). Faithfulness to IF+reset-by-subtraction+rate-coding varies per design; several (Spiker+, SyncNN) offer reset-by-subtraction as an explicit, user-selectable configuration, while others (FireFly) do not document reset polarity at all.

attributes.time_model: Synchronous, clock-driven; individual designs range from 100 MHz (Spiker) to 500-600 MHz (FireFly v2, highest reported among FPGA SNN accelerators surveyed).
attributes.neuron_models: Design-dependent: IF, LIF, first/second-order LIF (Spiker+ offers a library of six configurable models).
attributes.reset_semantics: Fully flexible in principle (synthesizable logic); Spiker+ and SIA natively support both hard and subtractive reset as selectable neuron variants; SyncNN implements explicit reset-by-subtraction (Vm -= Vth); FireFly's reset polarity is not documented in sources reviewed.
attributes.payload: Binary spikes in the designs surveyed.
attributes.weight_precision: Design-dependent, commonly 4/8/16-bit quantization.
attributes.on_chip_learning: Spiker-LL adds on-device local learning (STSF rule); most other designs surveyed are inference-only.
attributes.operator_coverage: Design-dependent (conv/dense/pooling support varies per accelerator).
attributes.toolchain: Design-dependent: Vitis HLS/SDSoC (SyncNN), custom VHDL generators (Spiker+), Xilinx Vivado synthesis (general).
attributes.availability: Any standard Xilinx/general FPGA development board; academic/open-source designs, not commercial neuromorphic products.

nodes.name: Rate / count coding
nodes.summary: The number of spikes over T timesteps represents a scalar value; under reset-by-subtraction and a fixed threshold, achievable spike counts {0,...,T} form an inherently uniform T-level quantizer, directly linking rate coding to uniform quantization-aware training.

nodes.name: Time-to-first-spike (TTFS) / latency coding
nodes.summary: Each neuron fires at most once; the timing of that single spike encodes the value. Achieves extreme sparsity but requires long training-time windows for useful spike-time gradients, and firing times must be quantized on real hardware (reintroducing a quantization floor). No soft reset of membrane potentials is needed for TTFS coding since neurons fire at most once.

nodes.name: Phase coding / weighted spikes
nodes.summary: Spikes are assigned a weight depending on which phase (position within a repeating K-timestep cycle) they occur in, typically powers of two (2^(K-1),...,2^0), producing a non-uniform (binary, exponentially-weighted) effective quantization grid -- the spike-domain analogue of non-uniform (e.g. logarithmic) quantization, in contrast to rate coding's uniform grid.

nodes.name: Burst coding
nodes.summary: A neuron may emit multiple spikes within or between a single simulation timestep when residual membrane potential after threshold crossing is large, rather than at most one spike per step; packs several rate-coding units of information into one step at the cost of within-step spike multiplicity.

nodes.name: Population coding
nodes.summary: A value is represented jointly by the activity pattern across a population of neurons (tuning curves, ensemble firing-rate vectors, or which neurons fire) rather than by one neuron's rate or timing; an orthogonal (spatial-multiplexing) axis that can co-occur with rate or temporal codes rather than a fourth encoding primitive.

nodes.name: Sigma-delta / graded / delta modulation
nodes.summary: Wraps a conventional activation with a delta encoder (transmits only the change since last transmitted value, above a threshold) and a sigma (running-sum) decoder, exploiting temporal redundancy in addition to spatial sparsity. Enabled at hardware level on Loihi 2 by native graded spikes carrying up to 24-bit signed integer magnitude.

nodes.name: Rank order coding (ROC)
nodes.summary: Information is carried entirely by the relative order in which a population's neurons fire (each firing at most once), not by rate or absolute timing; contrast-invariant and decoded via feedforward shunting inhibition. No published ANN-to-SNN conversion method targets ROC, because the rate/count-matching correspondence theorems underlying QCFS-style conversion are cardinal (magnitude-matching) while ROC's content is purely ordinal (a permutation).

nodes.name: Direct / analog / constant-current input encoding
nodes.summary: Real-valued input (e.g. pixel intensities) is applied as a constant analog input current to the first hidden layer at every timestep instead of first converting it to spikes; the first layer then performs a genuine (potentially multi-bit) MAC, forfeiting the accumulate-only efficiency the rest of the SNN enjoys, in exchange for materially improving conversion accuracy (Rueckauer 2017: CIFAR-10 ~59.8% Poisson vs. 83.6% direct current, same normalization).

nodes.name: Integrate-and-fire (IF) neuron, nonleaky
nodes.summary: V(t) = V(t-1) + z(t), spike when V(t) >= threshold, no decay term; the canonical neuron of the ANN-to-SNN conversion literature because, under reset-by-subtraction and constant/rate input, its time-averaged firing rate is an unbiased estimator of the ReLU activation it was converted from.

nodes.name: Leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron
nodes.summary: Adds an exponential leak term to the IF membrane update: V(t) = alpha*V(t-1) + z(t), alpha = exp(-dt/tau) < 1. Standard default on SpiNNaker (IF_curr_exp), Xylo, Spiker, and as a general Lava-DL/NIR primitive.

nodes.name: Current-based LIF (CUBA-LIF)
nodes.summary: Separates a first-order synaptic-current state u (its own decay tau_u) from the membrane-voltage state v: u(t) = alpha_u*u(t-1) + weighted-spike-input; v(t) = alpha_v*v(t-1) + u(t) + bias. Loihi's native baseline neuron model and the default neuron type in Lava-DL's SLAYER cuba block and NetX HDF5 schema.

nodes.name: Adaptive / threshold-adaptive neuron (ALIF)
nodes.summary: The firing threshold (or an equivalent subtractive after-hyperpolarizing current) increases after each spike and decays back toward baseline between spikes, implementing spike-frequency adaptation and LSTM-like long memory in recurrent SNNs. Native on BrainScaleS-2 (full AdEx analog circuit); on Loihi requires a 2-compartment AHP-current workaround.

nodes.name: Reset by subtraction (soft reset)
nodes.summary: V(t) = V(t-1) + z(t) - V_thr, carrying excess charge above threshold forward into the next integration window; proven by Rueckauer et al. to make the SNN's time-averaged firing rate converge exactly to the target ANN activation as T -> infinity, with error only from discrete sampling, not a persistent bias. Required by essentially all rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion theory (Diehl 2015, Rueckauer 2017, QCFS-family work).

nodes.name: Reset to zero (hard reset)
nodes.summary: V(t) forced to a fixed baseline (typically 0) whenever the neuron fires, discarding the residual charge epsilon = n*z - V_thr above threshold at every reset event; this residual is a systematic, input-dependent bias that compounds across layers and does not vanish with longer simulation time. Rueckauer et al.'s own CIFAR-10 ablation: switching only the reset mechanism (holding Poisson input and normalization fixed) improved accuracy by roughly 20 percentage points.

nodes.name: PASC-IF (spike-accumulation IF neuron)
nodes.summary: PASCAL's IF variant using spike accumulation and adaptive layerwise activation with soft reset and explicit inhibitory (negative) spikes; proven exactly equivalent to a QCFS-activation ANN with required timesteps T=L per layer (vs. QCFS's typical ~1024), rather than the classical hard/subtractive reset conventions used elsewhere in this survey.

nodes.name: SNN Toolbox
nodes.summary: Rueckauer et al.'s reference implementation of percentile-based weight/threshold-normalization ANN-to-SNN conversion with reset-by-subtraction IF neurons (Rueckauer 2017), the direct ancestor of the NxTF/Loihi pipeline; dormant since ~2021-2022 (last substantive release March 2021, last patches August 2022).

nodes.name: SpikingJelly
nodes.summary: PyTorch-based, full-stack SNN toolkit (Science Advances 2023) with CuPy/Triton-accelerated training, an ann2snn conversion module (rewritten into an FX-graph recipe framework, current flagship recipe no longer cites Rueckauer/Diehl), and export paths to Lava (lava_exchange), NIR (nir_exchange), and Lynxi. Actively maintained.

nodes.name: snnTorch
nodes.summary: PyTorch-native SNN training library (Eshraghian et al., Proc. IEEE 2023); snn.Leaky defaults to reset_mechanism='subtract' (soft reset); no official first-party deployment path to physical silicon was located, though third-party NIR export exists.

nodes.name: Norse
nodes.summary: PyTorch-based SNN library whose documented LIFCell/LIFRecurrentCell default to reset-to-zero (v_reset defaults to 0, hard-reset equation v=(1-z)v+z*v_reset); exports to NIR (norse.to_nir), with a documented caveat that round-trip export/import produces different spike patterns on identical input.

nodes.name: Sinabs
nodes.summary: SynSense's PyTorch-based SNN library with a first-party deployment path to Speck/DYNAP-CNN; from_model() defaults to MembraneSubtract() (reset-by-subtraction), matching the Speck hardware default; no dedicated BatchNorm-fold utility documented (users must fold/avoid BN before conversion).

nodes.name: Rockpool
nodes.summary: SynSense's second SNN library, targeting deployment to the Xylo family; mapper()/quantize_methods()/config_from_specification() pipeline deploys to XyloSamna/XyloMonitor on physical hardware or the bit-precise XyloSim simulator.

nodes.name: Lava (core)
nodes.summary: Intel's open-source, platform-agnostic Process/Process-model framework (CSP-style) with a low-level Magma compiler/runtime layer; the specific Magma components compiling to Loihi hardware are proprietary and gated to INRC members. Archived by Intel as of ~2026-05-13 ("stay tuned for announcements about our new SDK").

nodes.name: Lava-DL
nodes.summary: Intel's deep-learning library within Lava (lava.lib.dl): slayer (SLAYER 2.0 direct training), bootstrap (fast rate-coded-SNN training via ANN surrogate), and netx (HDF5-to-Lava-Process inference deployment). Archived alongside core Lava.

nodes.name: Nengo
nodes.summary: Implements the Neural Engineering Framework (NEF): analytically-solved decoding weights over spiking-neuron tuning curves, a fundamentally different construction from backprop-trained rate matching. NengoDL bridges to Keras/TensorFlow-style training and provides a Converter that swaps ReLU for spiking equivalents (rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion as one of its modes).

nodes.name: PyNN
nodes.summary: Simulator-independent Python API for building neuronal network models, runnable unmodified across NEURON, NEST, Brian, and, critically, two physical neuromorphic hardware backends: SpiNNaker (pyNN.spiNNaker via sPyNNaker) and BrainScaleS (pynn_brainscales.brainscales2). Does not itself define neuron reset semantics or time model -- inherited from whichever backend executes the model.

nodes.name: Brian2
nodes.summary: Neuroscience-first, differential-equation-defined neuron/synapse simulator with a Python front end and C++ code generation; GPU acceleration only via the separate Brian2GeNN bridge. Reaches deep converted CNNs only via SNN Toolbox as an external output backend, not through Brian2's own native API.

nodes.name: NEST
nodes.summary: Purpose-built for parallelized simulation of large, densely-connected recurrent networks of point neurons (biologically-realistic cortical-microcircuit scale); exposed as a PyNN backend for ANN2SNN pipelines built on top of it (e.g. via SNN Toolbox), but has no native CNN-conversion capability of its own.

nodes.name: hxtorch
nodes.summary: PyTorch interface to BrainScaleS-2 with two operating modes: non-spiking "hagen" mode (matmul/conv primitives executed directly on hardware as analog vector-matrix multiplication) and hxtorch.snn (LIF/LI spiking layers with hardware-in-the-loop training, CADC-sampled membrane traces injected into the PyTorch autograd graph).

nodes.name: BIDL (Brain-Inspired Deep Learning)
nodes.summary: Lynxi's open-source PyTorch-based training/deployment framework (with the Nanhu Research Institute) for LIF/LIF+ neurons and hybrid ANN+SNN "DSNN" networks (Conv/BN/pooling ANN layers interleaved with ConvLIF/ConvLIAF SNN layers); compiles via the Lyngor compiler and executes via the LynSDK runtime on Lynxi chips.

nodes.name: mlGeNN
nodes.summary: GPU code-generation-based conversion library adding explicit deep-CNN support atop GeNN; demonstrated VGG-16 and ResNet-34/20 converted and evaluated at real CIFAR-10 and ImageNet scale (VGG-16: 70.2% vs. 70.3% ANN baseline on ImageNet) -- but this is software/GPU simulation only (E5), not a neuromorphic ASIC target.

nodes.name: Neuromorphic Intermediate Representation (NIR)
nodes.summary: A unified graph IR (Nature Communications 2024) defining 17 computational primitives at the paper level (Input, Affine, Conv, LI, I&F, LIF, CuBa-LIF, etc.), read/written by 9 simulators and reaching 5 hardware platforms (BrainScaleS-2, Loihi 2, Speck, SpiNNaker2, Xylo). Verified directly against the reference implementation's neuron primitive source (nir/ir/neuron.py): NIR defines six neuron-adjacent primitives (CubaLI, CubaLIF, I, IF, LI, LIF); all three spiking primitives (IF, LIF, CubaLIF) specify reset identically as reset-to-a-fixed-value (v <- v_reset if spike else v, v_reset defaulting to 0). No NIR primitive specifies reset by subtraction -- this is a limitation of the specification itself, not of any one exporter. Hardware backends are explicitly permitted to simply ignore unsupported nodes rather than approximate them.

nodes.name: SpikingJelly lava_exchange
nodes.summary: SpikingJelly module implementing the documented pipeline SpikingJelly -> Lava DL -> Lava -> Loihi: data-layout conversion ([T,N,*] to [N,*,T]), IF/LIF-to-CubaLIFNode conversion via BlockContainer, export_hdf5() producing the same HDF5 schema lava.lib.dl.netx consumes.

nodes.name: SpikingJelly nir_exchange
nodes.summary: SpikingJelly's specific NIR import/export module; to_nir.py's _hard_reset() function raises NotImplementedError unconditionally whenever a neuron's v_reset is None (SpikingJelly's soft-reset convention), i.e. this specific exporter implementation never implements the subtractive-reset branch even though the exported IR format's own maintainers (NIR spec) do define one.

nodes.name: NxTF
nodes.summary: Intel's Keras-Model/Layer-derived DNN compiler within NxSDK for Loihi 1, distinct from the low-level NxNet API; trades NxNet's generality for CNN-focused compilation exploiting weight-sharing to compress models across cores. Explicitly built an interface between NxTF and SNN Toolbox (nxsdk_modules_ncl/dnn/.../snntoolbox). Superseded; INRC has directed users to Lava since 2022; intel-nrc-ecosystem/models carries a blanket "DISCONTINUATION OF PROJECT" notice.

nodes.name: DynapcnnNetwork (Sinabs mapper)
nodes.summary: Sinabs's DynapcnnNetwork(discretize=True) restructures a sequential Sinabs SNN into DynapcnnLayer objects (conv->spike->pool), discretizes weights to 8-bit and membrane/thresholds to 16-bit, auto-converts nn.Linear to 1x1 Conv2d and nn.AvgPool2d to SumPool2d, and places layers onto physical cores via chip_layers_ordering="auto" (raises an error if no valid placement fits per-core memory).

nodes.name: Rockpool Xylo mapper/quantizer
nodes.summary: Rockpool's mapper() extracts a hardware specification from a trained computational graph and DRC-checks it against Xylo's CuBa-LIF architecture constraints; quantize_methods (global_quantize / channel_quantize) quantizes weights/thresholds to 8-bit weights and 16-bit thresholds by default; config_from_specification() builds the final hardware configuration object.

nodes.name: sPyNNaker
nodes.summary: The PyNN backend (pyNN.spiNNaker) plus SpiNNTools execution engine that translates a PyNN network into an application graph, partitions it into a machine graph (~256 atoms/core given per-core SDRAM/DTCM budgets), places/routes it onto SpiNNaker cores (compressing routing tables to the ~1024-entry-per-chip router budget), loads compiled C executables, and extracts results after execution.

nodes.name: SpikingJelly ann2snn
nodes.summary: SpikingJelly's ANN-to-SNN conversion module, rewritten (2026) into an FX-graph "recipe" framework: converter.py is now pure orchestration delegating to recipes/ (rate_coding.py, local_threshold_balancing.py, qcfs.py, etc.). The legacy Converter (branch 0.0.0.0.14, VoltageHook/VoltageScaler/IFNode) is the version most external tutorials describe; current master's flagship LocalThresholdBalancingRecipe implements a 2024/2025 CVPR paper (Bu, Li, Yu) rather than Rueckauer 2017, with a >50-point ImageNet/ResNet-18 accuracy gap between the two normalization granularities at matched T=32.

nodes.name: BrainChip CNN2SNN / QuantizeML
nodes.summary: BrainChip's official pipeline: QuantizeML performs uniform, symmetric, zero-centered integer quantization-aware training/PTQ; CNN2SNN convert() maps the quantized Keras/ONNX model to an Akida-runtime-compatible .fbz model, folding BatchNorm and activation-quantization math into per-neuron static thresholds (with a rounded half-step offset) so those operations "are never performed during inference" as separate floating-point ops.

nodes.name: Quartz
nodes.summary: Lenz, Orchard, Sheik's time-to-first-spike (TTFS) ANN-to-SNN converter for Loihi, explicitly not rate-coded; states plainly that prior temporal-coding conversion methods had not been demonstrated on physical neuromorphic hardware before this work, and that "no soft reset of membrane potentials [is] needed" because TTFS neurons fire at most once.

nodes.name: NengoLoihi
nodes.summary: Backend compiling a Nengo network (built via NEF or via NengoDL ReLU-to-spiking conversion) onto Loihi; models discretized neuron activation profiles (LoihiLIF/LoihiSpikingRectifiedLinear classes) during training, respects the 1024-neurons/core limit, and ships both a Loihi emulator and a physical-hardware backend using Intel's proprietary NxSDK on a "superhost" wired to physical boards.

nodes.name: NxSDK
nodes.summary: Intel's Loihi 1 software development kit and register-level NxCore driver API; supported three high-level front ends (third-party Nengo, Intel's own NxNet, and NxTF) all compiling down through NxCore. Loihi-1-era; superseded by Lava for Loihi 2 per INRC's own 2022 migration guidance ("Older NxSDK models should be easily re-implemented in Lava").

nodes.name: samna
nodes.summary: SynSense's cross-chip developer interface and runtime environment ("the developer interface to the SynSense toolchain and run-time environment for interacting with all SynSense devices"): a Python API with a C++ core, applying device configuration objects (apply_configuration(cfg)) and streaming real-time event data through an EventFilterGraph of source/sink nodes and JIT-compiled filters.

nodes.name: Lava-DL NetX
nodes.summary: lava.lib.dl.netx.hdf5.Network(net_config=...) reconstructs a platform-independent HDF5 network description (produced by SLAYER/Bootstrap training or by SpikingJelly's lava_exchange export) as a runnable Lava Process graph, executable on CPU simulation or, for INRC members, physical Loihi 2 hardware by switching the RunConfig (e.g. Loihi2HwCfg vs. a CPU sim config).

nodes.name: Rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion
nodes.summary: The classical Diehl (2015) / Rueckauer (2017) methodology: train a continuous-valued ANN, then convert ReLU activations to IF-neuron firing rates over T timesteps via percentile-based weight/threshold normalization and reset-by-subtraction, proven to converge to the exact target activation as T -> infinity. The direct ancestor of QCFS-style conversion work and the reference lineage this thesis builds on.

nodes.name: Hardware-in-the-loop (HITL) training
nodes.summary: Forward pass executed on physical analog silicon; backward pass / gradient computed in software using an approximate (e.g. ReLU-derivative) model of the intractable hardware activation function, injecting hardware-measured quantities into the computation graph. The practical countermeasure BrainScaleS deployments use in place of relying on exact IF/LIF correspondence, which fixed-pattern mismatch and trial-to-trial analog noise make unattainable.

nodes.name: Image classification (static frames)
nodes.summary: MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet-scale classification of static images; historically the primary evaluation target of both classical and low-latency (QCFS-lineage) ANN-to-SNN conversion, and the task this thesis's own QCFS/QCFS+/QCFS++ tracks build on.

attributes.input_format: Static RGB/grayscale image datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet). Classical conversion papers compare Poisson-rate spike trains against direct/analog constant-current first-layer input; the QCFS lineage and its 16 audited descendants uniformly use direct/analog input rather than Poisson coding.
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Narrow but real for classical conversion: MNIST (0.66-0.79 mJ, 6.5-6.65 ms) and MobileNet-on-CIFAR-10 (8.52% error, 102 mJ, 340 ms, 1,753 cores/14 chips) via SNN Toolbox conversion + NxTF on physical Loihi 1; a rate-coded MNIST classifier on physical DynapCNN (98.79% accuracy, Bernoulli raster). By contrast, zero of 16 audited QCFS-lineage low-latency conversion papers (2022-2025, including QCFS itself) report any run on physical neuromorphic silicon; all are E5 GPU/PyTorch simulation, several with SynOps-based 'theoretical energy' tables that are frequently miscited as hardware results. Commercial (borderline-spiking) Akida reports 41 ms/215 mW/9 mJ per image classification.
attributes.platforms: Intel Loihi 1 (NxTF/SNN Toolbox conversion pipeline), SynSense DynapCNN (rate-coded raster via Sinabs), BrainChip Akida (commercial, delta/multi-bit event semantics rather than binary IF spikes).

nodes.name: Event-based vision
nodes.summary: Perception tasks (optical flow, tracking, pedestrian/vehicle detection) fed by native DVS/event-camera streams. The dominant published practice reconstructs the asynchronous stream into dense frames or voxel grids and hands it to a conventional CNN/Transformer; genuinely end-to-end sensor-to-spiking-chip pipelines with no frame reconstruction are a documented minority, concentrated in gesture recognition and simple closed-loop robot control.

attributes.input_format: Native asynchronous (x, y, t, polarity) address-event stream from commercial DVS sensors (iniVation DAVIS346/DVXplorer, Prophesee IMX636/GenX320). In the large majority of published pipelines this is reconstructed into dense frames or voxel grids before any neural network sees it; only the spike-based representation family among six taxonomized event-representation families is native to spiking hardware.
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Mixed. Frame/voxel-reconstruction pipelines dominate and run on GPU/workstation (E-RAFT, EvRT-DETR), embedded Jetson/RPi (AERO-VIS SLAM, EV-Catcher), or FPGA CNN accelerators (Vitis-AI DPU on Kria/Zynq boards, TrinitySLAM, EventBoost) -- none spiking. A small set of genuinely native sensor-to-spiking-chip deployments exist with no frame reconstruction: TrueNorth+DVS128 gesture (105 ms, <200 mW, 96.5% acc), SynSense Speck/Speck2f (DVS128 Gesture/Gait, real-time power as low as 0.70 mW), DYNAP-SE tactile localization and iCub motor control, SpiNNaker goalkeeper robot (6.5 ms, 85% acc, 7.15 W).
attributes.platforms: Native spiking: IBM TrueNorth, SynSense Speck/DYNAP-SE, SpiNNaker. Non-spiking (dominant): GPU/workstation, Jetson Orin/RPi 5, Xilinx Zynq/Kria Vitis-AI DPU.

nodes.name: Gesture recognition
nodes.summary: The single most consistently demonstrated genuinely end-to-end (sensor-to-spiking-chip) neuromorphic application in the survey, spanning DVS-based and EMG-based variants across nearly every major spiking platform, and the one task category where direct BPTT training, spike-time-gradient training, and rate-coded conversion have all independently reached physical silicon.

attributes.input_format: Native DVS event stream (TrueNorth, Speck, Loihi via SLAYER or via frame-preprocessed conversion) or surface EMG time series (Loihi EMG gesture classifiers).
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Yes, the strongest E1 application category found. TrueNorth+DVS128: 105 ms latency, <200 mW, 96.5% acc, 11 gestures, no host-side frame accumulation. Speck/Speck2f: 0.70 mW real-time power, +9.0% accuracy with 50% input masking. Loihi via SNN Toolbox conversion (Massa et al. 2020): 89.64% acc, 11.43 ms/frame classification + 150 ms preprocessing; this pipeline first accumulates DVS events into frames off-chip to train a conventional DNN, then converts -- not a native event-domain path. SLAYER-trained (spike-time-gradient) conv. SNN on physical Loihi 1 via NxTF: DVS Gestures, error/energy/delay all measured. Loihi EMG gesture classification: 90% acc, 983x/19x energy/latency gain vs GPU; 74% acc/5.7 ms/41 mW on Kapoho Bay. Loihi+ODIN/MorphIC tri-modal EMG+DVS sign-language fusion: 30-600x better energy-delay product vs GPU.
attributes.platforms: IBM TrueNorth, SynSense Speck/Speck2f, Intel Loihi (NxTF/SLAYER and SNN-Toolbox-conversion paths, +ODIN/MorphIC co-processor for EMG+DVS fusion).

nodes.name: Object detection
nodes.summary: Automotive and drone/robotics object detection built on event cameras or RGB video, overwhelmingly executed on conventional CNN accelerators (FPGA Vitis-AI DPU, GPU). No peer-reviewed report found of an object detector measured on physical rate-coded/IF spiking silicon; the one E1 spiking exception uses a non-rate-coded graded-spike (sigma-delta) conversion scheme on Loihi 2.

attributes.input_format: Event-camera frames/histograms (Prophesee Gen1/Gen4 accumulated into dense representations for YOLO-family detectors) or RGB video (Loihi 2 sigma-delta YOLOv3-style detector).
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Overwhelmingly non-spiking. Kria-Prophesee-Event-VitisAI and the FPGA-drone obstacle-avoidance pipeline both run YOLO-family detectors on a Xilinx Vitis-AI DPU (conventional systolic-array CNN accelerator; end-to-end 2.14 ms measured latency). 'Object detection on physical DYNAP-CNN/Speck: NOT FOUND' per the survey's dedicated search. The one genuinely spiking E1 exception is Sigma-Delta Neural Network conversion of a YOLOv3-style detector on physical Loihi 2 (16-chip VPX board): energy-delay product measured vs Jetson Xavier, using Loihi 2's native graded-spike payloads, not rate-coded IF neurons. Commercial Akida reports video object detection at 160 ms/78 mW/13 mJ.
attributes.platforms: Xilinx Vitis-AI DPU (non-spiking, dominant), Intel Loihi 2 (sigma-delta graded-spike conversion, E1), BrainChip Akida (commercial).

nodes.name: Keyword spotting and audio classification
nodes.summary: The strongest commercial, purpose-built, directly-trained-SNN deployment pipeline found in the survey (SynSense Xylo), which beats both Loihi and SpiNNaker2 on the same benchmark task in a head-to-head published comparison table.

attributes.input_format: Sampled audio time series (spoken-keyword and acoustic-scene benchmarks such as Aloha KWS, DCASE 2020), consumed by directly trained LIF-based SNNs, not converted from a static-frame ANN.
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Yes, E1. Xylo Audio 2 (SynSense, commercial): 95% acc on Aloha KWS, 6.6 uJ/inference dynamic energy, best-in-class in a published comparison table against GPU (29.67 mJ), CPU (6.32 mJ), Jetson (5.58 mJ), Loihi (0.27/0.037 mJ), SpiNNaker2 (0.0071 mJ); DCASE acoustic-scene classification on Xylo (28.4 uJ/inference dynamic). BrainChip Akida (commercial): 0.72 ms latency, >1,300 keywords/s, 62 uJ few-shot on-chip learning. Loihi keyword spotter: energy-per-inference lower than CPU/GPU/Jetson TX1/Movidius NCS at equivalent accuracy.
attributes.platforms: SynSense Xylo Audio 2 (commercial, directly trained via Rockpool), BrainChip Akida (commercial), Intel Loihi and SpiNNaker2 (research, cited secondarily within the Xylo benchmark table).

nodes.name: Biosignal decoding (EMG / EEG)
nodes.summary: Gesture/movement decoding from surface EMG and seizure/motor-imagery decoding from scalp EEG both reach physical Loihi silicon with consistently large measured energy/latency advantages over GPU baselines; grouped separately from vision-based gesture recognition because the input modality is a sampled physiological time series.

attributes.input_format: Sampled multi-channel physiological time series: surface EMG for gesture classification, scalp EEG for seizure prediction and motor-imagery decoding.
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Yes, E1 on Loihi/Loihi 2. EMG gesture classification (RSNN with DEXAT neurons, Nahuku 32): 90% acc, 0.37 mJ/inference, 983x/19x energy/latency gain vs GPU at batch=50. EMG 12-gesture classifier (NinaPro DB5, Kapoho Bay): 74% acc, 5.7 ms latency, 41 mW. EEG seizure prediction (Graded SNN, Loihi 2): 99.14% acc, 25.1 mJ/input, 21.6 segments/s throughput. EEG motor-imagery decoding on Loihi (Kapoho Bay/NxSDK): self-reported '95% more energy-efficient than DNNs at similar accuracy' in a repository README, not independently re-verified in the underlying survey pass.
attributes.platforms: Intel Loihi / Loihi 2 (research, INRC).

nodes.name: Olfaction (odor classification)
nodes.summary: The single most energy-efficient measured E1 Loihi result in the survey (single-shot learning, sub-millijoule per classification), but built on a hand-designed, locally-plastic biological circuit rather than gradient training; its algorithmic generalization claim is independently contested.

attributes.input_format: Wind-tunnel chemosensor readings mapped onto a biologically derived olfactory-bulb-model spiking circuit, learned online via local (one-shot) plasticity rather than backpropagation.
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Yes, E1, hand-designed circuit (not gradient trained). Physical Loihi, 72-core network: 92% single-shot accuracy versus roughly 3,000 samples/class needed by a DNN autoencoder for parity; <3 ms and <1 mJ per classification; scalability shown across 20-128 cores (time-to-solution independent of problem size). Caveat: an independent 2023 replication study found the underlying dataset suffers sensor drift and a non-randomized measurement protocol, and that a simple 8-line hash-table baseline matches or beats the Loihi network's accuracy under a proper train/test split -- the hardware latency/energy measurement itself is not invalidated, but the algorithmic generalization claim does not hold up.
attributes.platforms: Intel Loihi (research, INRC).

nodes.name: Robotics and closed-loop control
nodes.summary: The second-largest genuinely end-to-end (sensing-to-actuation) spiking-hardware application category after gesture recognition, spanning hand-designed motor-control circuits, gradient-trained spiking policies, and one hardware-adaptation (rescaling) step layered on top of gradient training.

attributes.input_format: Mixed: DVS event streams (goalkeeper robot), joint encoder feedback (iCub head-yaw P-controller), FSR+DVS sensor fusion (hexapod terrain adaptation), force-torque sensor streams (industrial peg-in-hole insertion), simulated proprioceptive state trained then ported to hardware (mapless navigation).
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Yes, E1 across several platforms. SpiNNaker goalkeeper robot: 6.5 ms response latency, 85% interception accuracy (balls up to 1 m/s), 7.15 W, DVS-to-SNN-to-servo fully closed loop, disconnected from any PC. SpiNNaker hexapod central-pattern-generator locomotion: 23 ms worst-case gait-transition delay. DYNAP-SE iCub head-yaw P-controller: closed-loop step response and target pursuit characterized (E2, no absolute power reported). Gradient-trained: mapless navigation SDDPG on Loihi (Kapoho Bay): 75x less energy per inference than DDPG on Jetson TX2; industrial force-controlled peg-in-hole insertion on Loihi 1 (1.8 ms) and Loihi 2 (1.5 ms, 53 uW dynamic energy vs 3,800 uJ CPU / ~100s uJ GPU), with a Loihi-specific 8-bit integer weight rescaling step applied on top of the trained policy before deployment.
attributes.platforms: SpiNNaker, SynSense DYNAP-SE, Intel Loihi / Loihi 2.

nodes.name: SLAM and localization
nodes.summary: SLAM/VIO is almost entirely a GPU/embedded-CPU/FPGA workload in the recent event-camera literature, with a single narrow hand-designed exception (unidimensional head-direction SLAM) reaching physical Loihi.

attributes.input_format: Event-camera streams, frame/voxel reconstructed for AERO-VIS, TrinitySLAM, EventBoost, and FRME; for the one spiking exception, odometry-style input to a biologically constrained head-direction/Bayesian-inference circuit.
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Almost none on spiking silicon. AERO-VIS (event-based inertial SLAM, closed-loop UAV): NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, TensorRT-compiled CUDA-graph inference. TrinitySLAM / EventBoost: Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA SoC, non-spiking hardware/software co-accelerated pipeline. FRME: FPGA algorithmic (event-warping) accelerator, not spiking. The single spiking exception: unidimensional SLAM (head-direction localization + mapping), hand-designed Bayesian-inference circuit on physical Loihi (Nahuku 8-chip board, 82 cores): 100x less dynamic power than GMapping on CPU, comparable localization accuracy.
attributes.platforms: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX / Xilinx Zynq FPGA (dominant, non-spiking); Intel Loihi (one hand-designed exception).

nodes.name: Optimization and constraint satisfaction
nodes.summary: Alongside olfaction, this is where the deepest and most consistently measured body of E1 Loihi evidence in the entire survey lives. Every instance found is a hand-designed spiking algorithm (Locally Competitive Algorithm for sparse coding/LASSO, SAT/CSP solving), never a gradient-trained network and never an ANN-to-SNN conversion.

attributes.input_format: Problem instances encoded directly into spiking-network structure and dynamics: sparse-coding dictionaries and LASSO regression coefficients (Locally Competitive Algorithm), CNF/DPLL-style Boolean formulas (SAT/CSP).
attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: Yes, E1, hand-designed (not gradient trained, not conversion). Spiking Locally Competitive Algorithm for sparse coding/LASSO on a Loihi predecessor chip: energy-delay-product improvement of more than three orders of magnitude vs. an Atom CPU, up to 5,760x EDP advantage at 32,256 unknowns; extended to physical Loihi 2 for both general LCA (orders-of-magnitude efficiency/speed advantage for large sparsity penalties) and convolutional sparse coding (latency and dynamic power measured vs. GPU, regime-dependent). SAT/CSP solving on Loihi: first reported CSP/SAT implementation on embedded neuromorphic hardware, static and dynamic power measured (power only; SAT solving is exact/deterministic, so no accuracy figure applies). Intel's own aggregated internal claims: 1,000-100,000x lower energy (LASSO), 2,800x lower energy and 44x faster (CSP/SAT/ILP/QUBO) vs. CPU, aggregated across these underlying papers.
attributes.platforms: Intel Loihi / Loihi 2 (research, INRC).

nodes.name: Direct training by surrogate gradient / BPTT
nodes.summary: Train an SNN end-to-end via backpropagation-through-time with a surrogate (smooth) derivative substituted for the non-differentiable spike function. The dominant paradigm behind SpikingJelly's SEW-ResNet/Spikformer/Spike-driven-Transformer image-classification lineage and STBP-derived robotics-control policies.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: Rarely for the ImageNet-scale image-classification lineage that defines this paradigm in the literature: zero of the headline surrogate-gradient/BPTT architectures audited (SEW-ResNet, STBP-tdBN, PLIF, TET, Spikformer/V2, Spikingformer, Spike-driven Transformer) have any confirmed physical-chip deployment; all report only theoretical SOP x 45nm-energy-constant estimates. Reaches silicon reliably when the workload is event-native and/or the training is hardware-aware: STBP-derived SDDPG mapless-navigation policy on physical Loihi (Kapoho Bay, 75x less energy/inference than DDPG on Jetson TX2); gradient-trained spiking force-control policy on physical Loihi 1/2 for industrial peg-in-hole insertion (1.5-1.8 ms latency, 53 uW dynamic energy); direct BPTT training of an IF-neuron CNN on physical Speck1 (N-MNIST, 98.50% on-chip accuracy, 180 uJ/inference). A SpikingJelly-trained object detector reached physical Loihi 2 (third-party 2026 preprint); a SpikingJelly-trained DVS128 Gesture network reached the physical CRI FPGA-based neuromorphic hardware (UCSD HiAER-Spike). Estimated well under 5% of SpikingJelly-based publications reach any physical chip at all.

nodes.name: Spike-time gradient methods (SLAYER / EXODUS / EventProp)
nodes.summary: Exact or near-exact gradient methods defined directly on spike timing rather than a surrogate derivative substituted into ordinary BPTT. The one direct-training lineage with a consistently exercised, vendor-maintained silicon path: SLAYER/Lava-DL to Loihi, and EventProp/mlGeNN to Loihi 2.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: Yes, routinely, via first-party vendor toolchains. SLAYER-trained CNN deployed via NxTF/NxSDK to physical Loihi 1 (DVS Gesture: latency and energy measured via a built-in performance probe). Lava-DL (SLAYER to NetX) PilotNet SDNN/LIF regression on physical Loihi 2: throughput 16.87-408.91 fps, full power/execution/memory/activity profiling. EventProp (exact-gradient BPTT) via mlGeNN to NetX to physical single-chip Loihi 2 with learned synaptic delays, on Spiking Heidelberg/Speech-Commands keyword spotting: 1.46-1.54 ms latency, 0.21-0.46 mJ energy, 18x faster and 250x less energy than an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano at batch=1. EXODUS itself (the training-speed algorithm underlying this lineage) has not been run on hardware in its own paper; deployment is exercised only downstream, via Sinabs to DynapCNN/Speck users.

nodes.name: Local learning and plasticity rules
nodes.summary: Hand-designed, biologically derived spiking circuits with local (often STDP-family or one-shot) on-chip plasticity rather than global backpropagation. This is where the largest and most rigorously measured E1 evidence base on Loihi actually concentrates (olfaction, SLAM, sparse coding/LASSO, SAT/CSP), not the surrogate-gradient/BPTT lineage that dominates the SpikingJelly ecosystem.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: Yes, extensively, and this is the single largest E1 body of Loihi application evidence found in the survey. Olfaction (Imam and Cleland, hand-designed circuit with one-shot local plasticity): 92% single-shot accuracy, <3 ms/<1 mJ per classification. Unidimensional SLAM (hand-designed Bayesian head-direction circuit): 100x less dynamic power than GMapping on CPU. Locally Competitive Algorithm for sparse coding/LASSO (hand-designed, provably convergent): more than three orders of magnitude EDP improvement vs. CPU, up to 5,760x at scale. SAT/CSP solving (hand-designed CNF/DPLL-style spiking encoding): first reported embedded-neuromorphic CSP/SAT implementation, power measured. iCub head-pose estimation (hand-designed path-integration circuit with on-chip plasticity, Loihi Kapoho Bay): RMSE 1.93-8.98 degrees, sub-10-ms real-time loop. Every one of these papers reaches Loihi because it was designed from the outset as a local, on-chip-compatible spiking algorithm, not because of gradient-based direct training -- this contrasts sharply with the gradient-trained surrogate/BPTT lineage, which reaches hardware far less often.

nodes.name: Hand-designed and hybrid fine-tuning
nodes.summary: Pipelines that combine a hand-designed or conventionally trained component with a lightweight, hardware-specific correction step, short of full hardware-in-the-loop backpropagation -- e.g. a chip-specific weight-rescaling/quantization step layered on top of gradient training, or direct-training results benchmarked head-to-head against conversion on the same chip.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: Partially, and documented only as a narrow middle ground between full HITL training and plain conversion. The SDDPG mapless-navigation paper applies a Loihi-specific 8-bit integer weight rescaling technique on top of its trained policy before deployment -- a hand-designed hardware-adaptation step, not backprop-through-hardware. The Speck1 paper's head-to-head, same-chip comparison shows direct BPTT training (180 uJ/inference, 98.50% on-chip accuracy) trading a modest energy cost for higher on-chip accuracy versus ANN2SNN conversion (141 uJ/inference, 86.17% in the same comparison table). No paper in the audited set performs genuine backprop-through-a-hardware-measured-forward-pass outside the BrainScaleS HITL lineage (already captured by the existing hardware-in-the-loop-training node); this node captures the lighter-weight calibration/rescaling middle ground documented for Loihi and DynapCNN/Speck deployments.

nodes.name: Binary spikes
nodes.summary: The default single-bit address-event spike payload: a bare source/target/timestamp event with no magnitude information. The payload type essentially all classical, low-latency, and quantization-aware rate-coded conversion work assumes, and the default mode on every reviewed digital spiking platform.

attributes.platforms: Native default on every reviewed digital spiking platform: Loihi 1 (binary spike is the only payload type), Loihi 2 (binary is still the default mode alongside its optional graded-spike payload), SpiNNaker 1/2, TrueNorth (purpose-built around a rate/count binary-spike scheme 'to simplify hardware implementation and enable highly energy-efficient large-scale neuromorphic systems'), and SynSense Speck/DYNAP-CNN (AER binary event stream).

nodes.name: Signed spikes
nodes.summary: A spike event whose payload or channel encodes sign, used to represent a negative delta or gradient rather than only a positive one. Native only on Loihi 2, via its signed graded-spike payload; every other reviewed platform fakes a signed quantity with two unsigned channels, doubling wiring or neuron cost.

attributes.platforms: Native only on Loihi 2, via up to 16-24 bit signed integer graded-spike payloads. Loihi 1 has no native negative-spike or signed-payload support: a fully on-chip spiking backpropagation implementation works around this by propagating the local gradient back twice through separate excitatory and inhibitory synapses, i.e. two unsigned channels standing in for one signed quantity, and the same paper notes that Loihi 2's graded spikes were introduced specifically to allow an efficient implementation for non-binary neural activations. TrueNorth has no bipolar spike from a single neuron either; its negative-threshold 'bounce' mode keeps a matched ON/OFF neuron pair in lock-step, again a dual-channel workaround, not a hardware-native signed spike. SpiNNaker's software-defined packet system has demonstrated a signed payload only for backward-pass error-gradient values (EventProp), not for standard forward-pass spikes; native support for ordinary signed SNN spikes is unconfirmed. No native signed-spike primitive was found for DYNAP-CNN/Speck, BrainScaleS-2, or FPGA designs in general.

nodes.name: Graded spikes
nodes.summary: A spike event whose payload carries a multi-bit (typically signed integer) magnitude rather than a bare 0/1, letting one event transmit a quantized activation delta directly instead of a count of binary spikes accumulated over T timesteps. Native to Loihi 2 via 16-24 bit signed payloads and dedicated sigma-delta microcode; the hardware feature underlying graded/sigma-delta ANN-to-SNN conversion.

attributes.platforms: Confirmed native only on Loihi 2 (up to 24 bits of signed integer magnitude, dedicated microcode; demonstrated in a fielded ANN-to-SDNN YOLO-KP object detector at 112 FPS, 5.0 ms latency, 20 mJ/frame). Loihi 1 lacks native graded spikes and can only approximate the mechanism via a two-compartment aLIF/sigma-delta neuron workaround at 2x compartment cost. SpiNNaker 2 supports large (128-bit) packet payloads and has demonstrated carrying signed floating-point values for backward-pass error gradients (EventProp), but this was not documented for a forward-pass sigma-delta activation encoding in the reviewed sources. No native graded-spike or sigma-delta support was found for SpiNNaker 1, DYNAP-CNN/Speck, BrainScaleS-2, TrueNorth, or FPGA designs in general (graded-spike support on FPGA is an achievable design choice, not an off-the-shelf feature).

nodes.name: Synchronous global tick
nodes.summary: Every core advances the same discrete time index in lockstep, enforced by an explicit barrier handshake (Loihi), a hardware timer interrupt (SpiNNaker), or a single global clock signal (TrueNorth, Tianjic). T is a logical/synchronization unit whose wall-clock duration is not fixed by the timestep count alone.

attributes.platforms_and_meaning_of_T: Loihi 1/2: fixed-size, discrete timesteps synchronized across cores (and, at scale, across the whole mesh) via explicit barrier messages over the asynchronous NoC; a timestep's real-world duration varies with spike traffic and congestion, and the paper stresses these algorithmic timesteps 'need not have a direct relationship to the hardware execution time.' SpiNNaker 1/2: a discrete timer interrupt, standardly 1 ms per timestep to match biological real time; this 1 ms convention is a software/API default, not a hardware limit, and sub-millisecond timesteps (e.g. 0.1 ms) have been used for higher accuracy at the cost of proportionally slower real-time factor.
