Xylo: a synchronous time-stepped architecture with a global time-step dt (master clock up to 50-100 MHz), genuinely executing one network update per global tick, up to 15 input events/channel and 31 output spikes/neuron processed within each tick. TrueNorth and Tianjic: per NeuroScale (Nature Communications 2025), TrueNorth uses an externally controlled ~1 kHz signal distributed to all hardware components to advance time for every component, and Tianjic uses a global clock for all its coordination processes including advancing time; both, together with Loihi and Loihi 2, advance through a single global barrier with no notion of one layer being ahead of another in tick count.

nodes.name: Asynchronous event-driven
nodes.summary: No global clock: computation is triggered directly by the arrival of an individual event at each block, which independently computes its output as soon as its input is available, drawing no running power while idle. T exists only at the boundary where a discrete-time raster is converted into a stream of individually timestamped events; on-chip, there is no notion of a timestep at all.

attributes.platforms: SynSense Speck: fully asynchronous logic built from cascaded blocks communicating via a request/acknowledge handshake, with no global or local clock signal on the convolutional compute path; measured 3.36 us for a single event traversing all 9 sCNN layers (about 0.37 us/layer), a hardware propagation delay rather than a multiple of any chosen simulation dt. Explicitly contrasted with clocked chips (Loihi 1/2, TrueNorth), which the same source states architecturally introduce a latency of one timestep dt per layer. DYNAP-CNN: same event-driven sCNN core as Speck. DYNAP-SE2: named and documented as a 'scalable multi-core dynamic neuromorphic asynchronous spiking neural network processor' in its own title.

nodes.name: Analog continuous time
nodes.summary: Physical analog circuit dynamics evolve continuously rather than in discrete algorithmic steps; component values, not a digital clock, set how fast the circuit runs relative to biological real time.

attributes.platforms: BrainScaleS-1: physical analog circuit time running about 10,000x faster than biological real time. BrainScaleS-2: physical analog circuit time at about 1,000x biological acceleration, with experiments scheduled into fixed wall-clock frames by an on-chip digital plasticity processor (PPU) and an explicit ~100-500 ns input interval in its non-spiking ('hagen') mode. DYNAP-SE2: fully analog, asynchronous, subthreshold-operated circuits with no global clock at all.

nodes.name: Single pass, T collapsed
nodes.summary: Execution collapses to one hardware pass over quantized, integer-only activations rather than a multi-timestep rate-coded simulation loop: a 'spike'/'event' is a nonzero (or newly-changed) quantized activation value, with no membrane potential accumulating over a user-specified T. The standard converted-CNN execution model on BrainChip Akida.

attributes.platforms: Confirmed for Akida's standard CNN2SNN/QuantizeML converted-CNN deployment path (the path essentially all published Akida results use): no user-exposed multi-timestep simulation horizon; scaling and quantized-activation math 'are never performed during inference' as separate floating-point ops because they are folded into the fire threshold at conversion time. Two independent papers describe this as the rate-code approximation of ReLU being squashed into one timestep, represented by a step-wise quantized ReLU. Some newer Akida layer types (BufferTempConv, TENN blocks) carry an internal temporal buffer/recurrent state for genuinely sequential data, which is a different (non-rate-coding) notion of time, not the rate-coding T this node otherwise describes.

nodes.name: Multi-compartment
nodes.summary: A neuron model split into two or more linked compartments holding separate state variables, used on digital chips as a workaround to implement mechanisms the native single-compartment neuron cannot express directly. On Loihi, the load-bearing use is reset-by-subtraction: because Loihi's native hard reset only zeroes the membrane, a second compartment configured to inhibit the first by exactly the threshold amount is needed to reproduce soft reset, doubling the compartment cost of every neuron that needs it.

attributes.platforms: Loihi 1/2: native multi-compartment support, used for three distinct workarounds in the reviewed literature: reset-by-subtraction (a second compartment subtracts the threshold from the first, since Loihi's native reset is hard-to-zero only), after-hyperpolarizing-current adaptive-threshold (AHP/ALIF) dynamics (up to 512 2-compartment neurons per core vs. 1,024 single-compartment), and the aLIF/sigma-delta neuron mapping (four state variables across two compartments, 2x compartment cost vs. a standard IF neuron). Loihi 2 inherits the same mechanism. BrainScaleS-2 documents the most extensively developed multi-compartment capability among all reviewed platforms, including genuine dendritic-spike (plateau-potential) computation, not merely a single-primitive workaround. No documented use of a genuine multi-compartment model was found for SpiNNaker (feasible via a custom software neuron, not documented as used).

nodes.name: Static frames
nodes.summary: Conventional dense RGB/grayscale image input (MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet-scale datasets), the default representation of both the classical/QCFS-lineage ANN-to-SNN conversion literature and any converted-CNN deployment (Akida, Loihi via SNN Toolbox/NxTF).

attributes.usage: The image-classification-static workload is static-frames by definition. Classical and low-latency conversion papers compare Poisson-rate spike trains against direct/analog constant-current first-layer input on exactly this representation; the QCFS lineage and its audited descendants uniformly use direct/analog input. A frame-camera or a frames-from-events reconstruction can equally feed this representation once a dense tensor exists.

nodes.name: Native event stream
nodes.summary: The raw, unreconstructed asynchronous (x, y, t, polarity) address-event stream from an event camera or other neuromorphic sensor, consumed directly by an event-driven spiking chip with no intervening frame buffer.

attributes.usage: A documented minority path relative to frame/voxel reconstruction (see frames-from-events). Genuine sensor-to-spiking-chip examples with no frame reconstruction: TrueNorth+DVS128 gesture recognition (105 ms latency, <200 mW, 96.5% accuracy, no host-side frame accumulation), SynSense Speck/Speck2f (real-time power as low as 0.70 mW), DYNAP-SE tactile localization and iCub motor control, SpiNNaker goalkeeper robot (6.5 ms, 85% accuracy, 7.15 W).

nodes.name: Sampled time series
nodes.summary: Sampled sequential/time-domain sensor data (audio, surface EMG, scalp EEG, IMU, force-torque, encoder feedback) consumed by directly trained or hardware-in-the-loop-trained SNNs, rather than a static-image ANN converted to spikes.

attributes.usage: Keyword spotting and audio classification: Xylo Audio 2 (95% acc Aloha KWS, 6.6 uJ/inference), Akida (0.72 ms latency, >1,300 keywords/s), Loihi keyword spotter. Biosignal decoding: EMG gesture classification on Loihi (90% acc, 0.37 mJ/inference; 74% acc/5.7 ms/41 mW on Kapoho Bay), EEG seizure prediction on Loihi 2 (99.14% acc, 25.1 mJ/input). Robotics and control: force-torque-driven peg-in-hole insertion on Loihi 1/2, proprioceptive-state-trained mapless navigation (SDDPG) on Loihi. Hardware-in-the-loop training on BrainScaleS-1/2 also operates on time-series-style spike trains injected into the analog substrate.

nodes.name: Frames reconstructed from events
nodes.summary: A dense frame or voxel-grid tensor built by accumulating an asynchronous event stream over a fixed time window, then handed to a conventional (non-spiking) CNN or Transformer. Documented as the dominant, default practice in the event-vision deep-learning literature, not a minority special case, and no spiking route in this survey passes through it: every downstream deployment observed from this representation targets GPU, embedded CPU/Jetson, or a conventional FPGA CNN accelerator (Vitis-AI DPU), never a spiking chip.

attributes.prevalence: A 2025 NeurIPS paper states plainly that 'most event-based deep learning pipelines convert asynchronous events into dense representations (particularly voxel grids) before neural network processing.' A 2023 IEEE TPAMI survey taxonomizes event representations into six families (image-based, surface-based, learning-based, voxel-based, graph-based, spike-based); only the last is native to spiking hardware, and the other five all collapse the stream into a dense tensor. Concretely: Prophesee's own production object-detection/tracking pipeline accumulates events into a frame buffer before calling a TorchScript/CPU-or-CUDA network; its ev-ultralytics YOLO fork trains on event histograms explicitly substituting for RGB frames; automotive datasets (Gen1, 1-Megapixel/Gen4) ship pre-converted to frame/histogram form for COCO-style evaluation. Even a nominal 'Loihi + DVS' deployment (Massa et al. 2020) is frames-from-events under the hood: events are pre-accumulated into frames off-chip to train a conventional DNN, which is only then converted for on-chip inference -- the DVS-to-frame step itself never runs on spiking hardware.
attributes.downstream_compute: GPU/workstation (E-RAFT, RAFT-spline/bflow, EvRT-DETR -- explicitly CPU-bound for data loading even with GPU inference), embedded CPU/Jetson/Raspberry Pi (AERO-VIS SLAM, EV-Catcher), or conventional FPGA CNN accelerators (Kria-Prophesee-Event-VitisAI, the CVPR-W 2025 FPGA-drone obstacle-avoidance pipeline on a Xilinx DPU, TrinitySLAM, EventBoost) -- none of these targets are spiking.

nodes.name: Tracking and motion estimation
nodes.summary: Optical flow, feature tracking, and motion estimation from vision (usually event-camera) input. Overwhelmingly a GPU/workstation and embedded-CPU/Jetson workload in the surveyed literature; essentially absent from genuine neuromorphic silicon, in contrast to gesture recognition and simple closed-loop robot control.

attributes.physical_silicon_deployment: NOT FOUND on physical spiking silicon in this survey. E-RAFT, RAFT-spline/bflow (dense optical flow, DSEC/MVSEC benchmarks) train and evaluate on CUDA GPUs with no embedded or neuromorphic deployment. rt_of_low_high_res_event_cameras requires a CUDA GPU library, with 'real-time' meaning GPU real-time. IBM's Neuromorphic Optical Flow work (CVPR 2023) explicitly frames the problem as needing model simplification because full-accuracy optical-flow networks are 'prohibitive for application at the edge or in robots,' itself evidence that the default/baseline compute target is a GPU. High-Speed Altitude Regulation with Neuromorphic Camera computes optical flow on a Raspberry Pi 5 (embedded CPU, not a spiking chip). The survey's own rough count places optical flow and tracking outside the small minority of tasks (gesture recognition, simple closed-loop robot control) where genuine spiking/neuromorphic silicon is used at all.

nodes.name: Event camera (DVS)
nodes.summary: A commercial dynamic-vision-sensor (DVS) chip outputting an asynchronous stream of (x, y, timestamp, polarity) address-event tuples over USB3 or MIPI CSI-2, plus, on some models, a secondary low-bandwidth raw AER pin header intended for direct neuromorphic-hardware interfacing. Event-based/neuromorphic in its sensing principle, but its primary production interface is the same USB3/MIPI path used by conventional CMOS image sensors.

attributes.output: Asynchronous (x, y, t, polarity) address-event tuples (AER at the wire-protocol level, or a proprietary packed format such as Prophesee EVT2.1/EVT3.0 at the interface level). None output spikes destined for a spiking-neuron substrate by default.
attributes.interfaces: iniVation DAVIS346: USB 3.0 primary, plus an optional 16-pin raw AER connector explicitly for direct FPGA/neuromorphic-hardware interfacing (cannot carry frames or IMU data). iniVation DVXplorer: USB 3.0 only, no raw AER breakout. Prophesee IMX636 (EVK4): MIPI CSI-2/SLVS at the die, bridged to USB-C for the evaluation camera. Prophesee GenX320: MIPI D-PHY or 8-bit parallel/CMOS-Parallel-Interface (CPI), with the vendor's own documentation stating the CPI/AER output path 'is mainly destined for integration with neuromorphic systems' -- implying the default MIPI path is not.
attributes.platforms_consuming_it_directly: SynSense Speck (DVS array co-integrated with the DYNAP-CNN spiking core on one die, no external interface needed), IBM TrueNorth via an external DVS128 sensor, SpiNNaker via an external silicon-retina DVS. The vendor's own flagship reference designs (Raspberry Pi 5, Jetson Orin NX, STM32 Discovery kits) target conventional processors, not spiking chips.

nodes.name: Frame camera
nodes.summary: A conventional CMOS/global-shutter image sensor producing dense RGB or grayscale frames at a fixed frame rate, delivered over USB3 or MIPI CSI-2. Not event-based; the source of the static-frames representation for classical/low-latency/quantization-aware ANN-to-SNN conversion and for any converted-CNN deployment, and, for benchmark datasets such as MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet, often not a physical sensor at all but a pre-captured, distributed dataset.

attributes.usage: Feeds the static-frames representation directly. The image-classification-static workload is evaluated almost entirely on pre-captured frame datasets rather than a live frame camera in the audited conversion literature.

nodes.name: Silicon cochlea
nodes.summary: An event-based analog/mixed-signal audio front end that converts sound directly into a spike train (rather than a sampled PCM waveform), used as the sensing front end behind spike-domain audio benchmarks such as the Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD) and Spiking Speech Commands (SSC) datasets.

attributes.platforms: SHD/SSC (silicon-cochlea-derived spike trains) are the benchmark behind the mlGeNN/EventProp keyword-spotting pipeline measured on physical single-chip Loihi 2 (1.46-1.54 ms latency, 0.21-0.46 mJ energy, 18x faster and 250x less energy than a Jetson Orin Nano at batch=1). A separate digital neuromorphic learning processor (ReckOn, 28 nm) demonstrates end-to-end on-chip learning directly on SHD (spiking-cochlea input): 90.7% accuracy, 1-word keyword spotting, 5.3 pJ/synaptic-operation peak efficiency.

nodes.name: Microphone
nodes.summary: A conventional audio sensor delivering a sampled PCM waveform, the input modality behind most keyword-spotting and speech benchmarks in the survey; not event-based, but the resulting sampled time series is what a directly trained SNN (Xylo, Loihi) or Akida's converted keyword spotter consumes.

attributes.platforms: SynSense Xylo has a documented Real-Time operating mode driven autonomously by the chip's internal timestep counter and 'live microphone/sensor input,' with output read via XyloMonitor -- the clearest documented case of a physical spiking chip consuming a live microphone feed directly. Xylo Audio 2's benchmarked keyword-spotting result (95% acc on Aloha KWS, 6.6 uJ/inference) and the Loihi/Akida keyword-spotting results in the survey are trained and evaluated on recorded speech-command datasets, i.e. microphone-sourced sampled audio, rather than silicon-cochlea event streams.

nodes.name: Tactile sensor
nodes.summary: A touch/e-skin sensor whose output is converted into DVS-like or spike-domain events before reaching a spiking chip: a GelSight optical-tactile front end generating marker-motion events (GelNeuro), or a fiber-Bragg-grating (FBG) e-skin generating touch events (DYNAP-SE tactile localization).

attributes.platforms: GelNeuro (2026): a GelSight optical-tactile front end feeds DVS-like marker-motion events directly into a physical Speck2f DYNAP-CNN spiking CNN, no frame reconstruction; 96.3% accuracy on 15-class texture recognition, 80 ms inference window, 19.6 mW board-level active power, over three orders of magnitude lower than conventional CPU/GPU baselines. DYNAP-SE tactile localization (Ortone et al. 2026): an FBG-based e-skin drives an SNN mimicking early somatosensory processing, implemented on physical DYNAP-SE (4,096 adaptive-exponential analog neurons); 5.33 +/- 0.15 mm localization error (only 8% worse than software), 185 uW median inference power, 8.7 uW resting power.

nodes.name: Chemical sensor array
nodes.summary: A wind-tunnel/chemosensor array whose readings are mapped onto a biologically derived olfactory-bulb-model spiking circuit; the sensing front end behind the survey's single most energy-efficient measured E1 Loihi result.

attributes.platforms: Feeds the olfaction workload directly: physical Loihi, 72-core network, 92% single-shot accuracy versus roughly 3,000 samples/class needed by a DNN autoencoder for parity, <3 ms and <1 mJ per classification. An independent 2023 replication study found the underlying dataset suffers sensor drift and a non-randomized measurement protocol, which undercuts the algorithmic generalization claim without invalidating the hardware latency/energy measurement itself.

nodes.name: IMU and analog sensors
nodes.summary: Proprioceptive and analog physical sensing that is neither a camera nor a microphone: IMU/inertial data, joint encoder feedback, force-torque sensors, and surface-EMG electrodes. Feeds the time-series representation for robotics/control and biosignal-decoding workloads rather than a vision or audio pipeline.

attributes.platforms: Robotics and control: force-torque sensor streams drive industrial peg-in-hole insertion on physical Loihi 1 (1.8 ms) and Loihi 2 (1.5 ms, 53 uW dynamic energy); simulated proprioceptive state trained then ported to hardware drives SDDPG mapless navigation on physical Loihi (Kapoho Bay, 75x less energy per inference than DDPG on Jetson TX2), with a Loihi-specific 8-bit integer weight-rescaling step applied to the analog-sensor-scaled inputs before deployment. Biosignal decoding: surface EMG electrodes drive gesture classification on physical Loihi (RSNN/DEXAT neurons, 90% acc, 983x/19x energy/latency gain vs GPU; 74% acc/5.7 ms/41 mW on Kapoho Bay).

nodes.name: No sensor (dataset or solver)
nodes.summary: Workloads with no physical transducer at all: a problem instance (a sparse-coding dictionary, a CNF/DPLL-style Boolean formula) is encoded directly into spiking-network structure and dynamics, or a benchmark dataset is loaded from disk rather than sensed live.

attributes.platforms: Optimization and constraint satisfaction is the clearest example: the Locally Competitive Algorithm for sparse coding/LASSO and SAT/CSP solving on physical Loihi/Loihi 2 both encode the problem instance directly into the network (sparse-coding dictionaries and LASSO coefficients; CNF/DPLL-style Boolean formulas) with no sensor in the loop at all -- more than three orders of magnitude EDP improvement vs CPU for LCA, and the first reported embedded-neuromorphic CSP/SAT implementation with power measured.

nodes.name: Classical conversion
nodes.summary: The founding threshold-balancing/weight-normalization ANN-to-SNN conversion methodology (Cao 2015, Diehl 2015, Rueckauer 2017, Sengupta 2019, and five further core algorithm papers). None of the nine core algorithm-proposing papers report any physical hardware execution; hardware validation of the methodology exists only in separate, later systems papers that adopt the conversion pipeline as an input rather than introducing it.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: 0 of 9 core algorithm-proposing papers audited (Cao 2015, Diehl 2015, Rueckauer 2017, Sengupta 2019, Han/Srinivasan/Roy 2020 RMP-SNN, Han/Roy 2020 TSC, Deng/Gu 2021, Li et al. 2021, Ho/Chang 2021) report any run on physical neuromorphic silicon; all 9 are E5, and several report SynOps-based or per-operation analytical energy/complexity estimates that are frequently miscited downstream as hardware results. Physical E1 results for this methodology exist only in downstream, separately authored systems papers that adopt the SNN Toolbox pipeline as an input: SNN Toolbox to NxTF on physical Loihi 1 (CIFAR-10 MobileNet, 8.52% error, 1,753 cores across 14 chips) and SNN Toolbox to sPyNNaker on physical SpiNNaker 1 (MNIST LeNet, 98.20%).

nodes.name: Low-latency conversion
nodes.summary: The QCFS-lineage of conversion papers that reduce T from hundreds/thousands of timesteps to single digits via improved activation clipping, potential initialization, or membrane-residual correction, evaluated at CIFAR/ImageNet scale. Audited against physical-hardware deployment: zero of sixteen papers report any run on physical neuromorphic silicon.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: 0 of 16 QCFS-lineage/low-latency conversion papers audited (QCFS, OPI, SRP, COS, SlipReLU, Burst Spikes, SNM, Fast-SNN, Dynamic Confidence, QFFS, SEENN, CS-QCFS, Adaptive Calibration, PASCAL, NeuroFlex, SpikeConverter) report E1 or E2 physical-silicon results; 15 of 16 are pure E5 software simulation (including SynOps-based theoretical-energy tables), 1 (NeuroFlex) is E4 hardware-model/RTL synthesis. A narrower, independently re-audited 13-paper citation-direction sample confirms 0 of 13 name a chip in the context of an experiment they themselves ran; only QCFS itself cites (but does not reproduce) two prior physical-hardware deployment papers in related work, correctly and non-abstract-only.

nodes.name: Quantization-aware conversion
nodes.summary: Conversion methods that fold per-layer bit-width/quantization choices directly into the timestep or threshold search, e.g. QAC's proof that the timesteps T of a soft-reset IF-neuron SNN are mathematically equivalent to the quantization level 2^n of a matched-precision quantized ANN activation, converting a mixed-precision-quantized ANN into a mixed-timestep SNN. Shares the same audited hardware-deployment position as low-latency conversion, and its own hardware-mapping discussion is explicitly qualitative rather than an executed run.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: 0 of 16 (and 0 of 13 in the narrower citation-direction sample), the same audited population as low-latency-conversion since bit-width/timestep-equivalence methods (QAC, AdaFire, CS-QCFS, PASCAL) are drawn from and audited alongside the QCFS-lineage low-latency set. QAC itself performs no RTL synthesis, cycle-accurate simulation, or accelerator implementation of any kind; its own hardware-mapping section is a purely descriptive/qualitative discussion that explicitly predicts pipeline stalling if its heterogeneous per-layer timestep execution model were mapped onto real barrier-synchronized multi-core hardware -- TrueNorth, Loihi, Loihi 2, and Tianjic all advance through a single global barrier (per NeuroScale, Nature Communications 2025), so a hardware primitive for 'layer l runs for T_l ticks' does not exist on any of them.

nodes.name: Hardware co-designed conversion
nodes.summary: The only ANN-to-SNN conversion family in the survey with confirmed instances of a paper that both proposes a genuinely new conversion method and measures it on physical neuromorphic silicon, in both cases by abandoning rate coding for a platform-native code: Quartz (time-to-first-spike, on physical Loihi 1) and Brehove et al. (graded sigma-delta spikes, on physical Loihi 2).

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: Yes, E1, in both confirmed instances found in an extensive, deliberately adversarial search. Quartz (Lenz, Orchard, Sheik): a TTFS conversion method measured head-to-head against a rate-coded baseline on the same physical Nahuku 32 Loihi 1 board (static/dynamic/total power, latency, energy per inference; MNIST 0.9 uJ-s EDP vs 4.38 uJ-s for rate-coded, CIFAR-10 10.3 mJ-s vs roughly 34.9 mJ-s). Brehove et al. (ICONS 2026): a sigma-delta/graded-spike SDNN conversion measured on a physical Loihi 2 VPX board, field-deployed, energy-delay product measured (YOLO-KP object detector, 112 FPS, 5.0 ms latency, 20 mJ/frame). Both abandon rate coding for a platform-native code; no paper keeping plain rate coding while both proposing a new method and reaching silicon was found.

nodes.name: Hybrid SNN-ANN fine-tuning
nodes.summary: A pipeline that trains part of a network as a conventional ANN and part as an SNN (rather than a single end-to-end spiking network or a pure conversion), then deploys the hybrid model to physical hardware via a vendor toolchain bridge. Distinct from hand-designed-hybrid-finetuning's chip-specific calibration/rescaling step: here the hybridization is architectural (ANN layers plus SNN layers in one model), not a post-hoc correction on top of an otherwise pure SNN.

attributes.reaches_physical_silicon: Yes, E1. A 2024 report, 'Towards Efficient Deployment of Hybrid SNNs,' trains a network combining PyTorch/TensorFlow (ANN) components with SLAYER/Lava (SNN) components, then deploys to physical Loihi 1 via NengoLoihi (not the Lava power-measurement tools, which the paper states were unreliable at the time of writing); power (via the NengoLoihi profiler), core count, and spike-propagation-delay latency are all measured on-chip for an image-classification task.

nodes.name: QuantizeML
nodes.summary: BrainChip's quantization-aware-training / post-training-quantization front end for the Akida toolchain: converts a float Keras/ONNX CNN into an integer-only model using uniform, symmetric, zero-centered quantization with a FixedPoint/QFloat representation. Standard integer QAT, not threshold-balancing/rate-coding calibration; there is no weight-normalization pass calibrated to a target firing rate over a chosen T, and no iterative rate-coding simulation.

attributes.pipeline_position: First stage of BrainChip's official toolchain: MetaTF front end -> QuantizeML (this node) -> CNN2SNN -> Akida runtime. CNN2SNN's convert() then maps QuantizeML's quantized model to the Akida-runtime-compatible .fbz format, folding BatchNorm and activation-quantization math into per-neuron static thresholds so those operations are never performed during inference as separate floating-point ops.

nodes.name: Backend-specific graph
nodes.summary: The generic, non-portable internal model representation that sits between a training framework and a chip-specific compiler whenever no shared interchange format (such as NIR) is used. NxTF's Keras-derived DNN graph (Loihi), sPyNNaker's PyNN population/projection graph compiled by SpiNNTools into a per-core machine graph (SpiNNaker), the quantized Keras/ONNX graph QuantizeML hands to CNN2SNN's convert() (Akida), and Sinabs/Rockpool's mapper-specific network graphs (DynapCNN, Xylo) are all instances of this pattern: each is tied to its own framework and its own chip, and none is exchanged between vendors the way NIR is designed to be.

attributes.instances: Loihi: NxTF inherits from the Keras Model/Layer interface; no PyTorch bridge exists beyond a bespoke SNN-Toolbox-specific interface, so a PyTorch-trained model (e.g. from SpikingJelly) cannot reuse it. SpiNNaker: sPyNNaker's application graph is partitioned by SpiNNTools into a machine graph, placed and routed per-core, entirely framework-internal. Akida: QuantizeML's quantized Keras/ONNX model is not itself a portable exchange format; CNN2SNN's convert() consumes it directly and produces the Akida-specific .fbz file. DynapCNN/Xylo: Sinabs' DynapcnnNetwork and Rockpool's mapper() extract a hardware specification from a trained computational graph that is specific to that mapper, not portable to another chip.

nodes.name: Lava ProcessModels
nodes.summary: The Magma-layer execution runtime within Lava that actually runs a compiled ProcessModel on physical Loihi 2 hardware (the Loihi2HwCfg backend), reached from NetX-compiled network descriptions produced by SLAYER/Bootstrap training or by SpikingJelly's lava_exchange export when it succeeds. The Loihi-targeting Magma components are proprietary and gated to INRC members; the same ProcessModel abstraction can alternatively execute in a CPU/software simulation backend with no hardware involved. Archived by Intel as of 2026-05-13 with no further maintenance or patches accepted.

attributes.pipeline_position: NetX (compile) -> Lava ProcessModels (this node, run) -> Loihi 2 hardware, or a CPU/software ProcessModel backend for simulation. Physical Loihi 2 runs through this runtime are documented with full profiling (loihi2_profiler: throughput, power, execution, memory, activity) for Lava-DL SLAYER-trained networks (PilotNet SDNN/LIF regression, mlGeNN/EventProp keyword spotting).

nodes.name: SpiNNaker runtime
nodes.summary: The on-chip SpiN1API event-driven operating system plus the host-side SpiNNTools data-loading/execution/extraction pipeline that actually runs a placed-and-routed machine graph on physical SpiNNaker silicon: per-core neuron/synapse parameter blocks and synaptic-matrix data are generated on the host and loaded into each core's ITCM/DTCM/SDRAM, all cores are signaled to start together, SpiN1API then runs the compiled C executable on each core for the configured duration, and results are read back off-machine via the PyNN API. For SpiNNaker 2, the analogous py-spinnaker2 'experiment runner' partitions and executes single-chip or 48-chip systems, with a Brian2-based software-emulation fallback when no chip is available.

attributes.pipeline_position: sPyNNaker (compile/map, via SpiNNTools partitioning/placement/routing) -> SpiNNaker runtime (this node, data load + SpiN1API execution + readback) -> SpiNNaker 1/2 hardware.

nodes.name: Akida runtime
nodes.summary: BrainChip's on-device execution stage: CNN2SNN's convert() output (a .fbz model) is loaded and run either on physical Akida hardware (AKD1000/AKD1500/Akida Pico silicon) or on BrainChip's own software simulator, with no membrane potential carried across timesteps and no user-exposed T; a nonzero (or newly-changed) quantized activation is the unit the runtime treats as an event.

attributes.pipeline_position: CNN2SNN (compile) -> Akida runtime (this node) -> physical Akida hardware or software simulator. Measured on physical AKD1000-class hardware across four workloads: image classification 41 ms/215 mW/9 mJ, video object detection 160 ms/78 mW/13 mJ, keyword spotting 0.72 ms/>1,300 keywords/s, on-chip few-shot learning 1.5 ms/41 mW/62 uJ.

nodes.name: Host encoding and readout
nodes.summary: The host-side (non-spiking-core) encoding and readout step every reviewed digital platform still depends on: converting an input into the chip's native event/packet format before injection, and converting output spikes/counters back into a readable result after execution finishes.

attributes.platforms: Loihi: host I/O moves up to 160 million 32-bit integer messages per second between the host and the mesh in a documented LLM-on-Loihi-2 deployment. SpiNNaker: SpiNNTools generates per-core neuron/synapse parameter blocks and synaptic-matrix data on the host, loads them before execution, and reads spikes/recorded state back off-machine via the PyNN API after execution completes -- steps 4 and 6 of the documented compile-and-map pipeline. BrainScaleS-2: the on-chip digital plasticity processor (PPU) schedules experiments into fixed wall-clock frames fed from the host, with an explicit ~100-500 ns host-driven input interval in its non-spiking ('hagen') mode.

edges.mechanism: SNN-TB's Keras/PyTorch/Caffe/Lasagne-ingested, percentile-normalized, reset-by-subtraction IF conversion is bridged via a dedicated nxsdk_modules_ncl/dnn/.../snntoolbox interface into NxTF's Keras-derived DNN compiler.
breaks: framework boundary: NxTF is Keras-native; no generic PyTorch bridge exists, so SpikingJelly/PyTorch models cannot reuse this interface
edges.notes: Produced the clearest published rate-coded conversion result on physical neuromorphic silicon: CIFAR-10 8.52% error on Loihi 1 (413k neurons, 3M params, 1,753 cores/14 chips).

edges.mechanism: NxTF compiles the parsed, weight-normalized model down through the register-level NxCore API bundled in NxSDK.
breaks: NxTF/NxSDK never ported to or run on Loihi 2 per any source located; INRC's own 2022 guidance redirects members to Lava for Loihi 2

edges.mechanism: NxSDK's NxCore register-level API programs Loihi 1 hardware directly; reset-by-subtraction is realized via a two-compartment soft-reset trick (a silent "soma" compartment inhibits the firing compartment by the threshold amount) because Loihi 1's native reset is hard-to-zero.
breaks: doubles the number of compartments (hence neurons/memory) consumed on-chip; NxTF's own authors list built-in soft reset as a desired future hardware feature specifically to remove this cost

edges.mechanism: spikingjelly.activation_based.lava_exchange converts SpikingJelly's [T,N,*] multi-step tensors to Lava DL's [N,*,T] layout and its IF/LIF neurons into a unified CubaLIFNode representation via BlockContainer, en route to export_hdf5().
preserves: 8-bit weight quantization matching Loihi's native precision
breaks: HARD BLOCKS soft reset: raises ValueError('lava only supports for v_reset == 0!') at five separate call sites whenever v_reset != 0.0, so a network trained with SpikingJelly's own ann2snn soft-reset default (v_reset=None) cannot be exported as-is; also blocks LIF decay_input=True and any bias term in exported Conv2d/Linear layers; only IF and LIF neuron types supported
edges.notes: One of the most consequential breaking edges in the survey: SpikingJelly's own ann2snn module defaults to soft reset (matching SNN Toolbox/Rueckauer), but SpikingJelly's own Lava export path refuses that exact output.

edges.mechanism: export_hdf5() produces the same platform-independent HDF5 network-exchange schema that lava.lib.dl.netx.hdf5.Network consumes.
preserves: hard-reset-only semantics carried through from lava_exchange
breaks: no soft-reset path exists upstream, so nothing downstream can recover it without retraining

edges.mechanism: netx.hdf5.Network(net_config=...) instantiates a runnable Lava Process graph from the HDF5 description; switching the RunConfig (Loihi2HwCfg vs. CPU sim) targets physical Loihi 2 for INRC members.
breaks: entire path frozen: Lava/Lava-DL/NetX archived by Intel ~2026-05-13 ("All Lava repositories are archived... stay tuned for announcements about our new SDK"), successor SDK unannounced; documented worked examples (lava_mnist) report a CPU-simulated Loihi accuracy (0.9863), not a confirmed physical-silicon run

edges.mechanism: SpikingJelly's nir_exchange submodule traces the model graph (nirtorch-style) to produce a NIR-compatible export/import path, distinct from the Lava-specific lava_exchange route.
breaks: only IF/LIF-family neurons handled; higher-order/adaptive neuron types not covered by this exporter

edges.mechanism: to_nir.py's _hard_reset() helper converts a SpikingJelly neuron's reset configuration into NIR's IF/LIF/CubaLIF primitive, which specifies only a fixed-value reset (v <- v_reset if spike else v, v_reset defaulting to 0).
preserves: hard-reset (v_reset != None) neuron export, faithfully represented since NIR's spiking primitives only encode fixed-value reset
breaks: BREAKS reset-by-subtraction entirely, and correctly so given the target format: NIR's own primitive specification (six primitives -- CubaLI, CubaLIF, I, IF, LI, LIF, verified directly against nir/ir/neuron.py) defines reset identically for all three spiking primitives as reset-to-a-fixed-value; no NIR primitive specifies reset by subtraction. SpikingJelly's exporter raises NotImplementedError('NIR does not distinguish soft reset.') whenever v_reset is None -- this is correct behavior given that NIR cannot represent that semantics at all, not an implementation bug in SpikingJelly's exporter
edges.notes: The limitation is in the NIR specification itself, not in SpikingJelly's exporter: NIR, the broadest interchange format surveyed (nine simulators, five hardware platforms), cannot represent reset-by-subtraction at all, so no exporter targeting NIR -- regardless of implementation quality -- could preserve it.

edges.mechanism: snnTorch's NIR export traces its neuron classes (which internally implement subtract-reset, confusingly called "hard reset" in snnTorch's own terminology) into NIR primitive nodes.
breaks: historically exported v_reset=0 for subtract-reset neurons, silently losing the hard-vs-soft distinction (tracked in snnTorch PR #388, 'add missing v_reset parameter on export', and a related reset-mechanism refactor PR documenting the terminology confusion)

edges.mechanism: norse.to_nir() traces a Norse model (whose documented LIFCell default is reset-to-zero) into NIR primitive nodes.
preserves: hard-reset (v_reset=0) neuron export, matching Norse's own default
breaks: third-party verification found Norse's own export-import round trip produces different spike patterns on identical input (checked with Norse 1.1.0) -- the path is functional but not numerically stable

edges.mechanism: py-spinnaker2's NIR importer maps Conv1d/Conv2d/Flatten/Affine/Linear/CuBaLIF/IF/LIF/SumPool2d nodes onto SpiNNaker2 processing elements (import only; does not yet support exporting arbitrary nodes back to NIR).
breaks: asymmetric capability: SpiNNaker2's own backend supports BOTH reset-by-subtraction and reset-to-zero, a hardware/software capability the formal NIR primitive spec itself does not expose, so the extra capability must be configured outside NIR's own fields

edges.mechanism: hxtorch.snn (and the related jaxsnn) both write to and read from NIR for LIF/LI neuron layer graphs.
preserves: LIF/LI node structure with CADC-sampled state
edges.notes: NIR's own cross-platform validation found faithful agreement for feedforward IF/LIF models but diverging accuracy for recurrent (CuBa-LIF, SRNN) cases, attributed to platform-specific discretization choices, requiring platform-dependent quantization-aware training to recover accuracy.

edges.mechanism: Sinabs both writes to and reads from NIR (sinabs.from_nir / to_nir), used e.g. to import a NIR graph and re-target it for Speck deployment.
breaks: unknown -- no source located confirming whether Sinabs's own reset-by-subtraction default survives a NIR round-trip cleanly, given NIR's hard-reset-only formal primitive spec

edges.mechanism: Rockpool both writes to and reads from NIR, targeting SynSense's Xylo hardware family.
Lava-DL reads (import only) NIR graphs.
breaks: write direction not supported

edges.mechanism: sinabs.from_torch.from_model(model, reset_fn=MembraneSubtract(), spike_layer_class=IAFSqueeze) replaces ReLUs with IF spiking layers; DynapcnnNetwork(discretize=True) then restructures the model into DynapcnnLayer (conv->spike->pool) objects and quantizes parameters to 8-bit weight / 16-bit membrane precision.
preserves: reset-by-subtraction (MembraneSubtract default matches hardware default return_to_zero=False)
breaks: no dedicated BatchNorm-fold utility (burden falls on the user to remove/avoid BN before calling from_model); nn.AvgPool2d is automatically rewritten to SumPool2d because 'spikes cannot really be averaged'; nn.Linear auto-converted to 1x1 Conv2d; Speck imposes a single, uniform threshold per spiking layer rather than per-neuron thresholds

edges.mechanism: hw_model.to(device=..., chip_layers_ordering='auto', ...) or the lower-level make_config(...) produces a samna configuration object with per-core cnn_layers[i] fields (weights, biases, destinations, threshold_high/low, leak_enable, return_to_zero).
breaks: chip_layers_ordering='auto' raises an error if no valid per-core memory placement exists (kernel/neuron/bias memory budgets differ per core)

edges.mechanism: samna applies the configuration object to physical silicon via apply_configuration(cfg); an EventFilterGraph chains source nodes, JIT-compiled filters (DvsEventCrop/Rescale/Decimate), and sink nodes for real-time event stream processing.
preserves: reset-by-subtraction (return_to_zero=False hardware register, the documented default)
edges.notes: Multiple published physical-silicon results: Nature Comms 2024 dynamic-SNN DVS-Gesture (81.0%/9.5mW vanilla vs. 90.0%/3.8mW dynamic), NIR-to-Speck N-MNIST tutorial (90.00% on-chip accuracy).

edges.mechanism: Same samna configuration/event-streaming mechanism as the Speck deployment, targeting the standalone DYNAP-CNN predecessor chip.
edges.notes: Face-recognition CVPRW 2019 demo: 98% recognition rate validated against software simulation, but the paper does not state accuracy was measured live on-chip, only power.

edges.mechanism: A trained Rockpool computational graph (LIFTorch/SynNet) is passed to mapper(), which extracts a hardware specification and DRC-checks it against Xylo's CuBa-LIF architecture constraints.
preserves: CuBa-LIF layer structure, per-layer synaptic time constants

edges.mechanism: quantize_methods (global_quantize/channel_quantize) quantizes weights/thresholds to 8-bit weights / 16-bit thresholds; config_from_specification() builds the final hardware config; XyloSamna/XyloMonitor deploy to the physical HDK in accelerated-time or real-time streaming mode with on-chip power recording.
preserves: subtractive reset (fixed hardware property, not a software switch)
breaks: multi-spike-per-timestep (up to 31 events/neuron/step) departs from the single-spike-per-step assumption of most conversion theory
edges.notes: Micro-power keyword-spotting (Aloha benchmark) on physical XyloAudio 2 HDK is a published E1 result: on-board current monitors sampled at 1280 Hz.

edges.mechanism: SNN-TB's spiNNaker_target_sim.py module builds PyNN-based Conv2D/DepthwiseConv2D/Conv1D/dense/pooling layers from a parsed Keras/PyTorch model, handles weight scaling and Poisson-rate input encoding, and drives the sPyNNaker PyNN backend directly.
breaks: no SNN-TB-authored paper independently confirms classification results measured via this specific backend module on physical SpiNNaker silicon; the clearest physical result (Patino-Saucedo et al. 2019/2020, 98.20% MNIST on a SpiNNaker-103 machine) does credit SNN-TB conversion methodology but the exact code path used is not confirmed to be this module in every source

edges.mechanism: SpiNNTools partitions the application graph into a machine graph (~256 atoms/core given per-core SDRAM/DTCM budgets), places vertices onto cores, generates and compresses multicast routing tables to the ~1024-entry-per-chip router budget, loads per-core parameter blocks and compiled C executables, and signals synchronized execution start.
breaks: built-in sPyNNaker cell types (e.g. IF_curr_exp) use PyNN-conventional hard-reset LIF/IF semantics by default; reset-by-subtraction is achievable only by writing a bespoke C neuron model implementing a custom neuron_model_has_spiked() callback, not a built-in option
edges.notes: Earlier DBN-to-SNN conversion result on a single physical SpiNNaker 1 chip (Stromatias/O'Connor lineage): 95.01% MNIST accuracy, 0.3 W, ~20 ms latency, all measured on silicon.

edges.mechanism: pyNN.spiNNaker backend (via the sPyNNaker software stack) lets a PyNN-described model run unmodified on physical SpiNNaker boards.
breaks: no CIFAR-10-scale or larger (VGG/ResNet-class) rate-coded CNN was found run on physical SpiNNaker 1 or 2 silicon via any documented path; all physical-hardware conversion results located are digit-recognition-scale or few-layer-CNN-scale

edges.mechanism: pynn_brainscales.brainscales2 backend, with hardware-specific setup() parameters (neuronPermutation, enable_neuron_bypass, initial_config for a stored calibration result), runs PyNN-described models on physical BrainScaleS-2 chips via queued EBRAINS/HBP Neuromorphic Computing Platform jobs.
preserves: standard PyNN model library, calibration-result loading

edges.mechanism: hxtorch.perceptron primitives execute non-spiking analog matrix multiplication on BrainScaleS-2 in the 'hagen' mode. Stradmann et al. measured physical-system latency and energy for a mobile ECG application on this path.
preserves: Quantized analog matrix multiplication with hardware-calibrated gains and measured output variation.
breaks: This path is a non-spiking ANN execution mode. It does not preserve spike-count or IF reset semantics from ANN-to-SNN conversion.
edges.notes: Physical measurement applies to the non-spiking analog mode. It must not be transferred to hxtorch.snn results.

edges.mechanism: hxtorch.snn runs spiking LIF and leaky-integrator layers on physical BrainScaleS-2, inserts sampled membrane traces into PyTorch autograd, and trains with surrogate gradients in the hardware loop. The published Yin-Yang demonstration reports on-chip classification accuracy.
preserves: Physical spike events and measured analog membrane traces enter the training computation graph.
breaks: The analog reset and device mismatch are not an exact digital reset-by-subtraction IF execution contract. The cited demonstration does not report hardware energy per inference or inference latency.
edges.notes: The paper reports 94.63 ± 0.7% Yin-Yang classification accuracy over 15 seeds on physical BrainScaleS-2. E2 applies to that claim; the separately measured non-spiking hagen path is E1.

edges.mechanism: Forward pass on physical BrainScaleS-1 wafer-scale hardware; backward pass computed in software using the ReLU derivative as an approximation of the intractable hardware activation function, over several tens of iterations.
breaks: naive rate-coded transfer without HITL correction collapsed accuracy from 97% (software) to 72% (+12/-10%); only after HITL correction did accuracy recover to 95% (+1/-2%), still short of the software baseline

edges.mechanism: Same HITL principle applied to BrainScaleS-2: forward pass on physical silicon (spiking LIF/AdEx mode or non-spiking 'hagen' mode), backward pass via calibrated linear/noise model or CADC-injected membrane traces.
breaks: non-spiking CNN mode: naive transfer degraded MNIST accuracy from 98.10% (6-bit software) to 92.13% (uncorrected on-chip); recovered to 98.01% only after HITL training; deliberately decalibrated networks recovered to 96.07% from 92.46% within a single HITL epoch

edges.mechanism: The classical conversion proof maps a ReLU activation to the time-averaged firing rate of an IF neuron under reset-by-subtraction and constant/rate input, converging exactly to the ANN activation as T -> infinity.
preserves: unbiased firing-rate estimator of the source ReLU activation

edges.mechanism: The converted network's activation values are represented as spike counts accumulated over T simulation timesteps, an inherently uniform T-level quantizer under a fixed threshold.
The IF neuron's firing-rate-to-activation correspondence proof is derived specifically under reset-by-subtraction dynamics.
preserves: unbiasedness of the firing-rate estimator as T -> infinity

edges.mechanism: The same IF neuron under reset-to-zero instead discards the residual charge epsilon above threshold at every reset event.
breaks: introduces a systematic, input-dependent bias term that compounds across layers rather than vanishing with more timesteps; Rueckauer et al.'s own CIFAR-10 ablation (holding everything else fixed) shows roughly a 20-percentage-point accuracy cost from this switch alone

edges.mechanism: TrueNorth's own Eedn training/deployment methodology is sometimes loosely associated with the same conversion literature, since both use backprop-trained networks mapped to spiking hardware.
breaks: BREAKS temporal rate coding entirely: Eedn encodes activation magnitude spatially, via the spike count across a population of redundant trinary-weighted neuron copies evaluated within a SINGLE 1 kHz tick, not via multi-timestep firing-rate accumulation the way Diehl/Rueckauer/QCFS-style conversion assumes; TrueNorth should not be cited as a hardware validation of temporal-rate-coded, IF-with-reset-by-subtraction converted SNNs

edges.mechanism: QuantizeML performs uniform symmetric integer quantization (x_int = clip(round(x/s), q_min, q_max)); CNN2SNN convert() maps the result to an Akida .fbz model, folding BatchNorm and activation-quantization math into a per-neuron static threshold computed once at conversion time (confirmed at the source level: y = x/act_step with a rounded half-step offset added to the threshold).
preserves: classification accuracy of the source quantized CNN (subject to a real accuracy cost at low bit-width without calibration/retraining, e.g. one independent study observed a drop from 90% to 30% before mitigation)
breaks: BREAKS essentially every primitive the rate-coded conversion literature assumes: no user-exposed multi-timestep simulation horizon T (collapses to a single feedforward pass); no membrane potential carried across timesteps; no reset-by-subtraction (static threshold-once instead of iterative subtract-and-carry); rate coding of an activation as a spike count over T is explicitly replaced by 'squashing the rate-code approximation of the ReLU into one time step', represented as a step-wise quantized ReLU
edges.notes: Independently confirmed by two unrelated groups that trained and deployed on real AKD1000 hardware (Ziegler et al. 2024 robotics paper; Lunghi et al. 2025 space-applications paper), not merely inferred from documentation.

edges.mechanism: Quartz's TTFS conversion compiles directly to physical Loihi hardware, compared against the rate-coded NxTF/SNN-TB baseline on the same datasets.
preserves: no soft reset required (neurons fire at most once)
breaks: accuracy trade-off vs. rate coding: CIFAR-10 25.14% error (Quartz, 1211 timesteps) vs. 8.52% error (rate-coded NxTF, 400 timesteps) -- Quartz trades accuracy for spike-count/energy efficiency at this scale

edges.mechanism: A Nengo network (built via NEF or converted from a Keras/TensorFlow model via NengoDL's Converter) is compiled by the NengoLoihi backend, which models Loihi's discretized neuron activation profiles (LoihiLIF/LoihiSpikingRectifiedLinear classes) during training and respects the 1024-neurons/core hardware limit.
NengoLoihi's hardware backend uses Intel's proprietary NxSDK on a 'superhost' connected to physical Loihi boards.
breaks: not rate-coded/QCFS-style conversion; built on NEF's analytically-solved tuning-curve encoding, a fundamentally different construction than backprop-trained rate matching
edges.notes: Published E1 results: 38x less energy than an architecturally identical network on an NVIDIA Quadro K4000 GPU for keyword spotting; two orders of magnitude less dynamic energy than CPU/GPU for a 7-DOF robot-arm adaptive controller (RMSE only 4.13% worse than the non-spiking analytic controller).

edges.mechanism: Lava-DL (lava.lib.dl) is built as a deep-learning library layered on core Lava's Process/Process-model API.

Models trained within lava-dl (via slayer for direct spike-based training or bootstrap for rate-coded surrogate training) are exported as platform-independent HDF5, which lava-dl's own netx submodule then loads for inference deployment.

preserves: CUBA-LIF hard-reset behavior (the reference PyLifModel process explicitly comments 'This is Loihi-1 compatible')
breaks: Lava's own v0.4.0 release notes state Lava did not, as of that release, support on-chip learning, Loihi 1, or a variety of connectivity compression features; entire stack archived by Intel ~2026-05-13 with no successor announced
edges.notes: E1 physical results exist for natively-trained (not rate-coded-converted) networks: PilotNet SDNN and audio-processing benchmarks measured on physical Loihi 2 (Shrestha et al. 2023).

edges.mechanism: BIDL's LIF/LIF+ neuron layers and hybrid ANN+SNN DSNN network descriptions compile via the Lyngor compiler and execute via the LynSDK runtime on Tianjic-lineage silicon.
preserves: LIF/LIF+ neuron dynamics; hybrid interleaved Conv/BN/pooling ANN layers with ConvLIF/ConvLIAF SNN layers
breaks: batch size restricted to 1 on-chip; only inference (not training) targets the chip; internal-iteration (GPU-friendly) vs. external-iteration (chip-native, timestep-driven) execution modes must be reconciled via a state-variable computational graph
edges.notes: Efficiency claims (DVS gesture, video, 3D medical, NLP) are framed at the algorithm/FLOPs-saved level, not board-measured watts/milliseconds, in the sources reviewed.

edges.mechanism: SpikingJelly's documentation lists a dedicated Lynxi-chip tutorial ('Inference on Lynxi chip') and a lynxi_exchange.py module in its deployment table.
breaks: not independently verified for on-chip numbers in this research pass; availability outside mainland China NOT FOUND

edges.mechanism: Cerebron explicitly builds its FPGA accelerator around the open-source SNN Toolbox conversion methodology as its offline training/conversion front end.
preserves: reset mode inherited from SNN Toolbox's own convention (implies reset-by-subtraction, not independently restated in Cerebron's own text)
edges.notes: MNIST 99.40% / 0.026 ms / 0.04 mJ per image; CIFAR-10 (thinner MobileNet) 91.90% / 10.63 ms / 14.88 mJ per image, measured on a physical Xilinx XC7Z100 implementation.

edges.mechanism: SyncNN implements a mathematically-proven-equivalent synchronous reformulation of the standard multi-timestep asynchronous IF-with-reset-by-subtraction execution: only the Poisson input-encoding layer runs for the full T-step window; downstream layers run once, computing the equivalent spike count via Vm/Vth division.
preserves: exact mathematical equivalence to standard rate-coded IF+reset-by-subtraction execution, explicit reset-by-subtraction (Vm[o] -= Vth), Poisson rate encoding
edges.notes: Measured across three physical Xilinx ARM-FPGA SoC boards (ZCU102, ZCU104, ZED): 99.6% accuracy, 13,086 FPS on MNIST.

edges.mechanism: PASC-IF's three-stage spike-generation datapath is integrated into the LoAS accelerator framework as a fully combinational circuit, exploiting LoAS's fully-temporal-parallel dataflow to remove the neuron's otherwise loop-carried temporal dependency.
preserves: PASCAL's exact ANN-SNN equivalence proof (T=L per layer)
breaks: departs from binary-only spike convention (explicit inhibitory/negative spikes) and from classical reset-by-subtraction (uses soft reset instead)
edges.notes: Concrete comparison in the paper: a task where the LoAS baseline needs T=32 timesteps and still shows ~5% accuracy degradation is matched by APEX (PASC-IF) at T=8, at 69.23 mJ/inference vs. LoAS's 181.76 mJ/inference at T=32 (61.9% energy reduction); the paper states LoAS would need T=1024 to match APEX's accuracy.

edges.mechanism: NeuroFlex extends PASCAL's layer-level lossless ANN/SNN equivalence to column-level hybrid execution, where individual output columns within a layer independently execute in ANN mode or PASC-IF SNN mode, chosen offline by a profiling-driven scheduler.
preserves: PASCAL's exact per-neuron integer-arithmetic equivalence proof (the proof depends only on local per-neuron integer arithmetic, so it survives column-level mixing)
breaks: not itself hardware; RTL synthesis + cycle-level simulation only, not fabricated silicon
edges.notes: Reports 98.6-99.3% PE-array utilization (VGG-16, ResNet-34, GoogLeNet) versus 71.0-83.9% for coarser layer-wise hybrid scheduling.

edges.mechanism: SNN-TB's brian2_target_sim.py module exports a converted model for direct simulation in Brian2.
preserves: reset-by-subtraction and percentile normalization as configured in SNN-TB
breaks: software simulation only; not a neuromorphic hardware target

edges.mechanism: pyNN's NEST backend lets a PyNN-described model run identically against the NEST simulator as one of PyNN's supported software targets.
breaks: no CNN-conversion-scale demonstration found for NEST; it is exposed only as a general-purpose point-neuron simulator, not a deep-CNN accelerator

edges.mechanism: Native DVS event streams (DVS128 Gesture/Gait, N-MNIST) are trained directly via BPTT (Sinabs+sinabs-exodus, SpikingJelly) and deployed to physical Speck/DYNAP-CNN and CRI FPGA hardware with measured on-chip accuracy and energy; the Speck1 paper's own head-to-head comparison found direct BPTT training gives higher on-chip accuracy than ANN2SNN conversion on the same chip.
preserves: event-native sparsity and temporal structure of the input stream
edges.notes: This is the strongest silicon-reaching pairing in the survey for event-based vision.

edges.mechanism: The only conversion-based event-vision deployment reaching physical silicon (Massa et al. 2020, Loihi DVS Gesture) first pre-accumulates DVS events into frames off-chip, trains a conventional DNN on those frames, and only then applies classical rate-coded ANN-to-SNN conversion (SNN Toolbox) before Loihi execution. No paper pairs a genuinely native (non-frame-reconstructed) event stream with rate-coded conversion on physical hardware.
breaks: native event-domain sparsity: the DVS->frame accumulation step happens off-chip before conversion, so the deployed pipeline is not end-to-end event-native despite running on physical Loihi
edges.notes: The single E1 exception (Massa et al. 2020) is frame-preprocessed, not native; the broader QCFS/low-latency conversion lineage evaluated on event-vision-adjacent tasks has zero physical-silicon deployments (16/16 audited papers are E5).

edges.mechanism: Classical threshold-balancing conversion (SNN Toolbox) transplants a trained ANN's ReLU activations onto IF neurons and deploys the resulting rate-coded network to physical Loihi 1 via NxTF for MNIST and MobileNet/CIFAR-10.
preserves: classification accuracy within a few points of the source ANN
edges.notes: Narrow: only small/shallow networks (MNIST-scale, MobileNet-on-CIFAR-10) have been shown on physical silicon; zero of the 16 audited QCFS-lineage low-latency conversion papers targeting this same task have reached any physical chip (all E5).

edges.mechanism: MNIST classification networks are run forward on physical BrainScaleS-1/-2 wafer-scale analog silicon, with a software backward pass (ReLU-derivative approximation, or calibrated linear/noise model) correcting for the intractable hardware activation function.
breaks: naive rate-coded transfer without HITL correction collapses accuracy: BrainScaleS-1 97% (software) to 72% recovered to 95% after HITL; BrainScaleS-2 non-spiking CNN mode 98.10% (6-bit software) to 92.13% recovered to 98.01% after HITL
edges.notes: Both existing HITL hardware edges (hitl-training-to-brainscales1/2) are for this same MNIST image-classification task; this edge makes the application-layer connection explicit.

edges.mechanism: A biologically derived olfactory-bulb-model circuit learns odor identity online via one-shot local plasticity rules, with no backpropagation or ANN-to-SNN conversion step anywhere in the pipeline.
edges.notes: One of the largest, most efficient E1 Loihi results in the survey; not gradient trained, not converted.

edges.mechanism: Unidimensional (head-direction) SLAM is implemented as a hand-designed, biologically constrained Bayesian-inference spiking circuit, not learned via gradient descent or converted from a trained ANN.
edges.notes: The sole spiking-hardware SLAM result found in the survey; every other SLAM deployment surveyed runs on non-spiking Jetson/FPGA hardware.

edges.mechanism: The Locally Competitive Algorithm (sparse coding/LASSO) and SAT/CSP solving are both hand-designed spiking algorithms whose dynamics provably converge to the target optimum; no training step (gradient-based or conversion-based) is involved at all.
preserves: provable convergence to the LASSO/sparse-coding fixed point
edges.notes: Together with olfaction and SLAM, this confirms the survey's finding that the largest E1 Loihi evidence body is hand-designed/local-plasticity work, not gradient-trained or converted networks.

edges.mechanism: Speck1's own benchmark trains an IF-neuron CNN directly via BPTT on N-MNIST and DVS-derived gesture-class data, then deploys the trained network to the physical chip.
preserves: on-chip accuracy close to the offline-trained baseline (98.50% on-chip vs 98.56% offline)
edges.notes: Direct BPTT training here outperforms ANN2SNN conversion on the same chip in accuracy (98.50% vs 86.17%), at a modest energy cost (180 uJ vs 141 uJ per inference).

edges.mechanism: Massa et al. 2020 trains a conventional DNN on frame-accumulated DVS Gesture data, then applies classical SNN Toolbox rate-coded conversion before deploying to physical Loihi 1.
preserves: classification accuracy of the frame-trained DNN
breaks: native event-driven processing: events are accumulated into frames off-chip before the DNN is trained, so the deployed network is not natively event-domain despite running on Loihi

edges.mechanism: A SLAYER-trained convolutional SNN (spike-time gradient, not surrogate-BPTT) is deployed via NxTF/NxSDK to physical Loihi 1 for DVS Gesture classification, with latency and energy measured on-chip.
preserves: exact spike-timing gradient signal through training

edges.mechanism: Xylo Audio 2's deployment pipeline (Rockpool) trains a quantized LIF-based SNN directly on keyword-spotting/acoustic-scene audio, with no ANN-to-SNN conversion step, then deploys to the physical commercial chip.
preserves: real-time inference accuracy above the Aloha KWS benchmark threshold
edges.notes: Best-in-class energy-per-inference among all compared devices (GPU, CPU, Jetson, Movidius, Loihi, SpiNNaker2) in the same published table.

edges.mechanism: EventProp (exact-gradient BPTT) trained via mlGeNN, exported through NetX, deploys a LIF network with learned synaptic delays to physical single-chip Loihi 2 for Spiking Heidelberg Digits / Spiking Speech Commands keyword spotting.
edges.notes: 18x faster and 250x less energy than an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano at batch=1.

edges.mechanism: EMG gesture-classification recurrent SNNs (DEXAT neurons) and the EEG seizure-prediction Graded SNN are gradient-trained networks deployed to physical Loihi/Loihi 2 with measured on-chip accuracy and energy.
preserves: classification accuracy within reported bounds of GPU baselines

edges.mechanism: The SDDPG mapless-navigation spiking actor network is co-trained end-to-end with a deep critic via gradient descent (an STBP extension) in simulation, then ported to physical Loihi; the industrial peg-in-hole force-control SNN policy is likewise trained via spiking RL and ported to physical Loihi 1/2.
preserves: closed-loop control performance of the trained policy
edges.notes: These are among the few directly (gradient-)trained Loihi robotics deployments found in the survey; most Loihi robotics work is hand-designed instead.

edges.mechanism: The iCub head-yaw P-controller, the hexapod central-pattern generator, and the SpiNNaker goalkeeper robot's perception-to-action mapping are hand-designed spiking circuits (with on-chip plasticity for iCub head-pose estimation), not trained via gradient descent.

The SDDPG mapless-navigation policy is trained via gradient descent in simulation but then passed through a hand-designed, Loihi-specific 8-bit integer weight rescaling step before physical deployment, closing the gap between the training-time and Loihi's native numeric format.
A YOLOv3-style detector is converted from a conventional ANN into a Sigma-Delta Neural Network using Loihi 2's native graded-spike payloads, and deployed to a physical 16-chip Loihi 2 VPX board.
preserves: detection accuracy of the source ANN
breaks: rate-coded IF representation: Sigma-Delta conversion uses 16-bit signed graded-spike payloads representing activation deltas, not binary spike counts under reset-by-subtraction, so this is architecturally distinct from QCFS-style rate-coded conversion
edges.notes: The only object-detection network found running on physical spiking silicon in the survey; no rate-coded/IF conversion of an object detector has been demonstrated on any physical chip.

edges.mechanism: Continuous-valued sensor/state inputs (proprioceptive state in the SDDPG mapless-navigation policy; force-torque readings in the industrial peg-in-hole task) are fed as constant/continuous input to the spiking policy network's first layer during gradient training, rather than being pre-encoded into a spike train.
preserves: full-precision continuous sensor readings at every timestep
edges.notes: Both deployments measured on physical Loihi.

edges.mechanism: Loihi 1 cores advance a shared algorithmic timestep via explicit barrier messages over the asynchronous NoC.
preserves: logical timestep ordering across all cores
breaks: fixed wall-clock duration per timestep (varies with spike traffic/congestion)
edges.notes: Barrier handshake, not a hardware clock; T is a synchronization unit.

edges.mechanism: Loihi 2 inherits the same barrier-synchronization mechanism as Loihi 1, adding pipelined and fall-through execution modes.
preserves: logical timestep ordering across all cores/chips
edges.notes: Confirmed structurally identical to Loihi 1's barrier mechanism.

edges.mechanism: A hardware timer interrupt, standardly 1 ms, advances every core's SpiN1API event loop together.
breaks: fixed 1 ms granularity unless reconfigured
edges.notes: 1 ms is a software/API default, not a hardware limit; sub-ms timesteps have been used.

edges.mechanism: Same timer-interrupt convention carried into SpiNNaker 2's py-spinnaker2 experiment runner.
Xylo genuinely executes one network update per global hardware timestep dt, driven by a master clock up to 50-100 MHz.
preserves: one-to-one correspondence between software T and hardware ticks
edges.notes: Opposite regime from DYNAP-CNN/Speck: T is a real hardware tick here, not a raster-to-event boundary artifact.

edges.mechanism: An externally controlled ~1 kHz signal is distributed to all TrueNorth hardware components to advance time for every component together.
edges.notes: Per NeuroScale's characterization of existing large-scale digital neuromorphic chips.

edges.mechanism: Tianjic uses a global clock for all its coordination processes, including advancing time.
edges.notes: Per NeuroScale's characterization of existing large-scale digital neuromorphic chips.

edges.mechanism: Speck's fully asynchronous logic triggers computation directly on event arrival, with no global or local clock on the convolutional compute path.
breaks: software num_timesteps is not one hardware update tick
edges.notes: Measured 3.36 us end-to-end single-event latency across all 9 sCNN layers.

edges.mechanism: Same event-driven sCNN core architecture as Speck.
preserves: no global clock on the compute path

edges.mechanism: DYNAP-SE2 is documented and named, in its own title, as an asynchronous spiking neural network processor.
Physical analog circuit dynamics run continuously at roughly 10,000x biological real time; acceleration is set by component values, not a digital clock.
breaks: exact digital-timestep correspondence

edges.mechanism: Physical analog circuit dynamics run continuously at roughly 1,000x biological real time, with the on-chip PPU scheduling experiments into fixed wall-clock frames.

breaks: multi-timestep rate accumulation

edges.mechanism: Loihi 1's neuron/synapse pipeline transmits and consumes only single-bit spike messages.
breaks: magnitude information

edges.mechanism: TrueNorth was purpose-built around a rate/count binary-spike scheme to simplify hardware implementation and maximize energy efficiency at scale.
SpiNNaker's multicast packet router forwards single-bit spike events by default.
SpiNNaker 2 retains binary spike events as its default forward-pass payload alongside its newer large-payload packet option.
Speck's AER event stream carries a single-bit polarity/address event with no magnitude payload.
Loihi 2's graded-spike payload includes a sign bit, natively representing a negative delta or activation value in a single event.

edges.mechanism: Loihi 2 microcode supports up to 24-bit signed integer graded-spike payloads, used directly by sigma-delta ANN-to-SDNN conversion.
breaks: accumulate-only binary-spike efficiency of the rest of the SNN literature
edges.notes: Demonstrated in a fielded YOLO-KP detector: 112 FPS, 5.0 ms latency, 20 mJ/frame.

edges.mechanism: A second compartment configured to inhibit the first by exactly the threshold amount reproduces reset-by-subtraction, since Loihi 1's native hard reset only zeroes the membrane; the same multi-compartment primitive is reused for AHP/ALIF adaptation and the aLIF/sigma-delta neuron mapping.
preserves: reset-by-subtraction semantics on hardware with a hard-reset-only native neuron
breaks: 1x compartment cost (doubles to 2x per neuron needing the workaround)

breaks: 1x compartment cost

edges.mechanism: An event camera's raw AER output can be consumed directly by an event-driven spiking chip with no frame buffer in between, e.g. Speck's on-die DVS array feeding its co-integrated DYNAP-CNN core.

edges.notes: The minority path relative to frames-from-events.

edges.mechanism: The overwhelming majority of published event-vision pipelines accumulate the event-camera stream into a dense frame or voxel-grid buffer over a fixed time window before any neural network sees it.
breaks: event-domain computation; native asynchronous sparsity

edges.mechanism: Wind-tunnel chemosensor readings are mapped directly onto a hand-designed, locally-plastic olfactory-bulb-model spiking circuit.
preserves: one-shot local-plasticity learning on raw sensor readings
edges.notes: 92% single-shot accuracy on physical Loihi; independently contested generalization claim (dennler2023-olfaction-replication).

edges.mechanism: Xylo's Real-Time operating mode is driven autonomously by live microphone input, with recognized-keyword output read via XyloMonitor; other benchmarked KWS results train and evaluate on microphone-recorded speech-command datasets.

edges.mechanism: Both reviewed tactile pipelines convert touch into DVS-like or spike-domain events before the spiking chip sees them: GelSight optical-tactile marker-motion events (GelNeuro) and FBG e-skin touch events (DYNAP-SE).
